    L3M: A Verifiable Harness and Runtime for Self-Extending and Self-Improving Agents

    L3M：面向自扩展与自我改进智能体的可验证框架与运行时

    Carson Eisenach, Robert Joseph George, Vincent Quenneville-Belair, Kate Gwimm, Dean Foster

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    L3M contributes a verifiable runtime that organizes persistent state, delegation, communication, and reversible tool use across agents and humans. Its agent decisions are incidental to the system design, with no substantive analysis of internal model mechanisms, composition, or reasoning.

    L3M 提供了一种可验证的运行时，用于组织智能体与人类之间的持久状态、委派、通信和可逆工具使用。智能体的决策在系统设计中只是附带因素；论文并未实质分析模型内部机制、组合能力或推理。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    The lasting gains in AI have come from methods that absorb more computation, and language models already scale computation within a call. Useful work, though, happens across calls: over hours or days, through tools and external systems, among many agents and the humans they work for, and increasingly through code the agents write themselves. Whether that work compounds is enabled by the harness around it, and the harness faces a constraint the model does not: of the three participants in such a computation, the human, the model and code, only the human's attention does not scale, so the computation can grow only if the human is not in every loop. L3M is a runtime built on that premise, written in Lean 4 so that one language implements the harness, states its invariants, and is the language agents extend it in. One computation spans humans, agents, models and code, and all of its state lives in Git: a rich state trajectory -- rather than a chat conversation -- is an object the runtime can resume, rewind, fork, compare and merge. Waiting, communication, delegation and undo are primitives, not patterns the model reasons through each time. When an agent works out a procedure, it can write it once as a sealed Lean program whose type is its permission request, and the harness offers it back as a tool -- machinery for the model to use. To take the human out of the loop, L3M uses reversibility to decide where that is safe: a tool's review tier follows from how far its effects can be undone, so agents act freely where the runtime can recover. Because the machinery can change, the properties that make this safe are stated as kernel-checked theorems about the code that runs. On Terminal-Bench, an untuned L3M reaches about two thirds of its (unsafe) shell-equipped pass rate using only safe (not needing human review) tools.

    中文

    AI 的持久进步来自能够吸纳更多计算量的方法，而语言模型已经可以在单次调用中扩展计算。然而，有用的工作发生在多次调用之间：持续数小时或数天，通过工具和外部系统，由许多智能体及其服务的人类共同完成，而且越来越多地依靠智能体自行编写的代码。此类工作能否累积进展，取决于其外围框架；该框架还面临模型本身没有的限制：在这种计算的三类参与者——人类、模型和代码——中，只有人类的注意力无法扩展，因此只有当人类不必参与每个循环时，计算规模才能增长。L3M 是基于这一前提构建的运行时，使用 Lean 4 编写，使同一种语言既能实现框架、陈述其不变量，也能供智能体用来扩展框架。一次计算涵盖人类、智能体、模型和代码，其全部状态都保存在 Git 中：丰富的状态轨迹——而非聊天对话——是运行时可以恢复、回退、分支、比较和合并的对象。等待、通信、委派和撤销都是原语，无须模型每次都通过推理来处理这些模式。智能体设计出某个流程后，可以将其一次性写成封装好的 Lean 程序，其类型就是权限请求；框架随后会将其作为工具提供给模型使用。为了让人类退出循环，L3M 根据可逆性来判断哪些操作是安全的：工具的审查等级取决于其影响能够撤销到什么程度，因此在运行时可以恢复的情况下，智能体可以自由行动。由于这些机制可能发生变化，确保安全的性质会以关于实际运行代码的定理形式陈述，并由内核检查。在 Terminal-Bench 上，未经调优的 L3M 仅使用安全工具（无需人工审查），就达到了其配备 shell 的（不安全）通过率的约三分之二。

    Self-Conditioning Enables Deep Sequential Reasoning in Flow Matching

    自条件机制使流匹配能够进行深层序列推理

    Zeyang Zhang, Linxiang Gao, Meiqi Gu, Xingyan Chen, Minrui Luo, Kaifeng Lyu, Tianxing He

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper analyzes how self-conditioning changes the expressive power and reasoning depth of iterative flow-matching models, with both complexity results and controlled visual-reasoning experiments. Its focus is reasoning mechanisms; iterative sampling relates to computation design, but the contribution does not primarily address broader system organization.

    论文分析了自条件机制如何改变迭代流匹配模型的表达能力和推理深度，并给出了复杂度理论结果和受控视觉推理实验。其重点是推理机制；迭代采样与计算设计有关，但该贡献并不主要涉及更广泛的系统组织。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Recent work has explored visual reasoning through image generation, where models solve visual-reasoning problems by directly generating solution images. Intuitively, iterative samplers such as flow matching are well suited to this task, since each sampling step may resemble one reasoning step. However, in this work, from a circuit complexity perspective, we show that this intuition is misleading. We prove that as long as the model outputs satisfy certain mild regularity conditions, the trajectory of the vanilla flow-matching sampler can be simulated by a constant number of sequential rounds of parallel model evaluations. Consequently, additional sampling steps cannot increase the expressive power of a constant-depth backbone model under the standard complexity-theoretic model of transformers. We then reveal that self-conditioning, which conditions the model on the previous step's estimate of the final image, plays a previously unrecognized role in removing this bottleneck. Controlled experiments on diverse visual-reasoning tasks show that flow matching with self-conditioning achieves higher accuracy and greater reasoning depth than vanilla flow matching, and its performance improves with more sampling steps. Theoretically, we prove that with self-conditioning, a constant-depth backbone can achieve expressive power equivalent to that of space-bounded Turing machines. Our study suggests a design principle for future visual reasoning research: carry more information between sampling steps, so that additional steps translate into deeper reasoning.

    中文

    近期研究探索了通过图像生成实现视觉推理，即模型直接生成解答图像来解决视觉推理问题。直观而言，流匹配等迭代采样器很适合这类任务，因为每个采样步骤可能类似一个推理步骤。然而，在这项工作中，我们从电路复杂度的角度表明，这种直觉具有误导性。我们证明，只要模型输出满足某些温和的正则性条件，原始流匹配采样器的轨迹就可以通过固定数量轮次的并行模型评估来模拟。因此，在标准的 Transformer 复杂度理论模型下，增加采样步数无法提升固定深度骨干模型的表达能力。随后我们揭示，自条件机制——即依据模型在前一步对最终图像的估计来对模型进行条件化——具有此前未被认识到的作用，能够消除此瓶颈。多种视觉推理任务上的受控实验表明，与原始流匹配相比，加入自条件机制的流匹配准确率更高、推理深度更大，并且性能会随着采样步数增加而提升。从理论上讲，我们证明，加入自条件机制后，固定深度骨干模型可以达到与空间受限图灵机等价的表达能力。我们的研究为未来的视觉推理研究提出了一项设计原则：在采样步骤之间传递更多信息，使额外步骤能够转化为更深层的推理。

    Beyond State Capacity: Why Retrieval Breaks in Mamba

    超越状态容量：Mamba 中的检索为何失效

    Nir Yarden, Amit Ben-Artzy, Roy Schwartz

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper investigates why Mamba retrieval fails, using gate interventions and layerwise probes to show that relevance information emerges too late for retrieval-critical gates. This directly advances mechanistic analysis of internal representations and selection; retrieval performance also connects to reasoning and recurrent model computation, but those are secondary to the mechanism studied.

    本文通过门控干预和逐层探测研究 Mamba 检索失效的原因，表明相关性信息出现得太晚，无法供检索关键层中的门使用。这直接推进了对内部表示和选择机制的机理分析；检索表现也与推理和循环模型计算有关，但这些方面相较于所研究的机制属于次要内容。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Mamba models underperform Transformers on in-context retrieval. This gap is usually attributed to Mamba's fixed-size recurrent state, which loses information as the context grows. We challenge this assumption by focusing on query-first retrieval, a setup in which the query precedes the context and state capacity should not be the binding constraint. We show that even in this setting Mamba lags substantially behind Transformers, despite its selection mechanism, which was designed to distinguish relevant content from distractors. We then demonstrate that the Mamba selection gates have sufficient control over the state updates to influence the model output: intervening on specific gates alone can swing accuracy between extremes. However, as gates are input-dependent, they require the incoming token's representation to encode its relevance to the query. We therefore probe token representations across layers, and find that the relevance signal emerges only gradually with model depth, and that the gates begin to reflect it only several layers deeper. Crucially, we find that gates in retrieval-critical layers are not yet aligned with relevance. The selection mechanism is thus expressive enough to solve the task, but it commonly operates on a relevance signal that has not yet arrived. Mamba's retrieval bottleneck therefore extends beyond state capacity: even when capacity is sufficient, the delayed emergence of relevance information across depth often prevents successful retrieval.

    Mamba 模型在上下文检索上的表现不如 Transformer。这一差距通常归因于 Mamba 的定长循环状态会随着上下文增长而丢失信息。我们对这一假设提出质疑，重点考察查询优先检索：在这种设置中，查询先于上下文出现，因此状态容量不应构成主要限制。我们表明，即使在这种设置下，Mamba 的表现仍显著落后于 Transformer，尽管它具备用于区分相关内容与干扰项的选择机制。随后我们证明，Mamba 的选择门对状态更新具有足够的控制力，可以影响模型输出：仅对特定门进行干预，就能使准确率在极端水平之间变化。然而，由于这些门依赖输入，它们需要输入词元的表示编码该词元与查询的相关性。因此，我们探测了不同层的词元表示，发现相关性信号只会随着模型深度逐步显现，而选择门要再深入数层才开始反映这一信号。关键的是，我们发现，检索关键层中的门尚未与相关性对齐。因此，选择机制的表达能力足以完成该任务，但它通常处理的是一个尚未到达的相关性信号。由此，Mamba 的检索瓶颈不止于状态容量：即使容量充足，相关性信息沿网络深度延迟显现，也常常会阻碍成功检索。

    Learning to Compute Is Not Learning to Retain or Reuse in Looped Transformers

    学会计算，不等于学会保留或复用：循环 Transformer

    Peilong Zhou, Hongtao Zhang, Yulong Huang, Cangyuan Li, Mingyu Chen, Ying Wang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper uses hidden-state interventions to distinguish computation, retention, and reuse in looped transformers, finding that correct computation does not ensure answers persist or remain reusable. This is a strong mechanistic study of iterative reasoning; the repeated block and state reuse touch compositionality and system design, but those are secondary rather than direct contributions.

    本文通过隐藏状态干预区分循环 Transformer 中的计算、保留和复用，发现正确计算并不意味着答案会持续存在或仍可复用。这是对迭代推理的有力机理研究；重复模块和状态复用涉及组合性与系统设计，但它们属于次要内容，并非直接贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Looped transformers compute by applying one block repeatedly, so they can run for more loops than they were trained with. Recurrent reasoners are known to overthink: iterating past the trained depth can turn a correct answer into a wrong one. Such a late error can reflect failed computation, loss of retention, or a state that later computation cannot reuse. We separate these cases in in-context Mealy-machine execution, where a simulator supplies intermediate targets and exact counterfactuals for hidden-state interventions. Models trained to answer at loop 32 are fully correct there but keep only 22% of these answers at loop 64. Retention depends on what training asks for: supervising one randomly chosen position per example, instead of always the last, keeps 99.8%, and randomizing the number of training loops also helps; truncating gradients, as in progressive training against overthinking, does not. The computation itself is exact: position $k$ is computed at loop $k$, and swapping its loop-$k$ hidden vector for the one from another input redirects every later position to that input's exact continuation (237/237 pairs in each of ten models). Retention, however, is not reuse. Even in models that keep nearly all answers, holding each position $k$ fixed from loop $k$ drops accuracy to 4--6%, whereas holding it from loop $k+4$ is harmless. A released recurrent maze network trained to avoid overthinking behaves the same way. Learning to compute is thus not learning to retain, and avoiding overthinking does not make a state reusable when its answer first appears.

    中文

    循环 Transformer 通过反复应用同一个模块进行计算，因此运行时可以循环多于训练时的次数。众所周知，循环推理器会过度思考：迭代超过训练深度可能使正确答案变成错误答案。这种后期错误可能反映计算失败、保留能力丧失，或后续计算无法复用某个状态。我们在上下文中的 Mealy 机执行任务中区分了这些情况；在该任务中，模拟器为隐藏状态干预提供中间目标和精确反事实。训练为在第 32 次循环时作答的模型在该循环次数下完全正确，但到第 64 次循环时只能保留这些答案中的 22%。保留能力取决于训练要求：每个样本随机监督一个位置，而不是总监督最后一个位置，可以将答案保留率提高到 99.8%；随机化训练循环次数也有帮助；而像针对过度思考的渐进式训练那样截断梯度则没有帮助。计算本身是精确的：位置 $k$ 在第 $k$ 次循环时被计算出来；如果将其第 $k$ 次循环的隐藏向量替换成另一个输入对应的向量，所有后续位置都会转向该输入的精确后续序列（在十个模型中，每个模型的 237 对样本均如此）。然而，保留并不等于复用。即使在几乎能保留所有答案的模型中，从第 $k$ 次循环开始固定每个位置 $k$，准确率也会降至 4--6%；而从第 $k+4$ 次循环开始固定则没有影响。一个为避免过度思考而训练并已发布的循环迷宫网络也表现出相同情况。因此，学会计算不等于学会保留，而避免过度思考也不会让状态在答案首次出现时就变得可复用。

We generate concise \textit{if--then} rules that express relations between perception to action and use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train Qwen2.5 and Llama3 models across four ToM benchmarks.     Recent work lets LLM agents evolve their own harness, up to the team itself. Yet in human groups, the same abilities achieve different outcomes under different social conditions. Borrowing the notion of scaffolding from developmental psychology, we investigate whether the social scaffolding of a self-evolving multi-agent system (MAS), namely its team composition and structure of interdependence (e.g., collaboration, conformity, or competition), shapes how the team evolves. We present AGORA (Agents Growing through Organization and Relational Arrangements), a framework that varies the two axes independently across three evolution mechanisms. Across web search, codebase understanding, and document QA, we find that (1) evolution alone rarely helps, while the right scaffolding surpasses a strong agent evolved alone by up to 25 points; (2) it does so by moving authority to the most capable member while the others step back; and (3) this member, having grown within the team, outperforms the same model alone.     JointServe: Serving Multi-Model Agents on Memory-Constrained GPUs

    JointServe：在内存受限的 GPU 上服务多模型智能体

    Daijin Hu

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    JointServe’s main contribution is a memory-aware serving system that coordinates model-weight and KV-cache residency, prefetching, and transfer scheduling for multi-model agents. Agent orchestration and planning are workload context, while the contribution directly advances model serving and memory management.

    JointServe 的主要贡献是一种面向内存的服务系统，它为多模型智能体协调模型权重和 KV 缓存的驻留、预取及传输调度。智能体编排和规划是其工作负载背景，而该贡献直接推动了模型服务和内存管理的发展。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    LLM agents are evolving from a single model calling tools to planners that orchestrate multiple expert models whose capabilities live in distinct weights. This shift breaks a hidden assumption of today's serving systems: that the working set of models fits in GPU memory. On the memory-constrained GPUs typical of private and edge deployments, naive whole-model swapping serializes weight transfer with computation and, without host-backed KV restoration, discards session state at a switch. We present JointServe, a serving system that treats weight shards and KV blocks as residency objects competing for one unified memory budget. JointServe exploits three structural properties of agent workloads (directed calls, gapped execution, and dual-state residency) to prepare models before they are called: an intent signal parsed from the caller's own output stream triggers prefetch during generation, partial k* residency reduces switching to incremental layers, and a preemptive transfer scheduler protects live-session KV with a guaranteed bandwidth share. A carve-out control step adjusts the weight/KV allocation as workload demands change. Evaluations show that JointServe reduces session completion time by 21.7% over the strongest whole-model swap baseline and stays usable in a crash regime where every whole-model swap baseline fails to finish (a 46-fold gap). On replayed SWE-bench, tau-bench, and OSWorld traces, it cuts session completion time by up to 49% and lifts SLO attainment from 2.8-24.5% to 76.8-100%.

This emphasis leaves the exploration behind a result difficult for researchers to understand, while long-running investigations face fragmented context and the risk of unsupported claims propagating across reasoning steps. We present Euler, a human-centered mathematical research system built around a shared, structured representation of the research process.     Sampling multiple chain-of-thought rationales from a language model can uncover correct solutions missed by a single attempt. However, these rationales are typically lengthy, making repeated autoregressive generation costly. Continuous latent reasoning offers a compact alternative, but point-valued methods condition repeated answer sampling on a single rationale, which can limit exploration of diverse paths and answer coverage. We thus propose rationale distribution distillation (RDD), training a conditional flow over fixed-length latent sequences by distilling from multiple textual reasoning paths. Furthermore, we expand the distillation targets through within-query mixup, interpolating between complete latent rationales for the same query. The flow nonautoregressively generates the entire latent sequence, and a frozen language model autoregressively decodes answers from sampled rationale contexts. We address this with a Sparse Transformer (ST): a 5-layer language model trained on TinyStories whose wide, TopK-sparse MLP forces neuron specialization. We show that ST neurons are highly interpretable: they outperform a loss-matched dense transformer by 43% on AutoInterp, and circuits of a median of 12 neurons suffice to reproduce individual model predictions. This testbed allows us to directly compare feature learning methods: Transcoder, which approximates the MLP input-output mapping, recovers ST's neuron vectors with 52.6% higher cosine similarity than Sparse Autoencoder, which only reconstructs outputs. We introduce manipulation units (MUs) as reusable operations, each defined by a local goal, an initi?ation condition, and observable success and failure criteria. MUs are learned and verified individually. During execution, consecutive MUs remain coupled through shared environ?ment dynamics. We formulate MU-Structured Manipulation (MUSM) and realize it through MU-Centric Orchestration (MUCO). Given language and vision, MUCO constructs an MU sequence, matches each MU to compatible policy models in a frozen capability registry, and dispatches the model with the highest calibrated success rate. Visual verification checks MU outcomes against success and failure criteria and governs transitions, enabling retry or fallback to another model from the current state without re-executing verified MUs.     Reasoning over infinitely long documents is becoming a reality with recurrent memory agents. However, increasing context length exacerbates the trade-off between reasoning performance and inference efficiency. Inspired by Kahneman's account of fast and slow thinking, we propose MemDuet, a dual-process memory framework that learns to coordinate a small language model for fast, parallel evidence selection from raw context chunks (System 1) with a large language model for memory-update verification and memory updates in document order (System 2). Experiments on diverse long-context reasoning benchmarks (RULER-HQA, LongBench v2, and 2WikiMultiHopQA) demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off as context length grows.     ENGLISH

    Transformers can perform in-context reinforcement learning without parameter updates. However, existing theoretical constructions often require context sizes that grow with the number of sampled transitions, leading to increasing memory costs in large-scale problems. This raises a fundamental scalability question: how much context is intrinsically necessary to carry out such learning? We answer this question for fixed-policy TD evaluation. We show that, with a shared linear decoder, the minimum context dimension required to exactly reproduce the first $L$ TD iterates is the Krylov dimension induced by the sampled transitions. When the available context dimension $m$ falls below this threshold, exact reproduction is no longer possible. In this regime, we characterize the optimal approximation error and show that it decays as $\Theta(\gamma^m\max\{1,1/(m(1-\gamma))\})$ where $\gamma$ is the discounting factor. Moving from representation complexity to actual memory cost, we characterize the optimal retained memory for exact continuous representations as $\Theta(nk_L)$ and show experimentally that on a sampled task whose exact rank is full but whose numerical rank is small, a context accurate to $10^{-2}$ is $88.7\%$ smaller than the sparse sufficient statistics of TD. Finally, we establish the learnability of the shared executor through pretraining by proving global convergence of an auxiliary objective over effective attention parameters under suitable task diversity. Experiments across diverse TD evaluation problems validate parameter recovery and the predicted context--accuracy tradeoff.

    Memory systems for persistent personal agents must move beyond isolated memories, maintaining both personal memory about whom they serve and procedural memory about how to act. Crucially, in harness-based personal assistance, procedures or skills are inherently user-conditioned: personal context determines which procedures apply, how they are instantiated, and when they should change. Existing benchmarks typically emphasize either personal or procedural memory, leaving their interaction underexplored. We introduce PraxisMemBench, a harness-based benchmark for persistent personal assistance across daily-life and work trajectories, where personal and procedural memory evolve together and later tasks depend on both. Experiments show that maintaining two memory types separately is insufficient, with completion dropping from single-type to interdependent dependencies (84.6% to 77.9%). More broadly, across existing methods, relation-related failures increase from early to late sessions as interaction history grows (59.8% to 72.9%), revealing a continual-maintenance challenge: writing correct memories is not enough if their evolving content and organization cannot be preserved for later retrieval. To address this, we propose PraxisMem, which uses privileged joint-state supervision to internalize the ability to maintain memory content and organization into the memory manager, with location-aware GRPO and dynamic residual-routed OPSD. PraxisMem reaches 40.78% overall Session Success Rate, compared with 20.60% for Claude Code's native memory.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper introduces compute-responsive data selection for post-training models to use additional test-time reasoning more effectively, and evaluates gains across compute budgets and settings.     本文提出计算响应型数据选择方法，通过后训练让模型更有效地利用额外的测试时推理，并评估其在不同计算预算和设置下的收益。本文侧重于推理能力的发展；样本选择并未实质涉及组合泛化，而测试时计算只是训练方法所处的背景，并非系统方面的贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Reasoning language models increasingly rely on test-time compute scaling, yet most existing work studies how to allocate inference computation while treating the model itself as fixed. We ask a complementary question: can reasoning models be post-trained to make better use of a given amount of test-time compute, and which examples are most useful for this goal? Our key observation is that reasoning problems differ substantially in their response to additional computation. Some are already solved under limited compute, others remain unresolved even after further reasoning, while a distinct subset changes from complete initial failure to success when additional reasoning is provided. We call these compute-responsive (CR) examples and introduce Compute-Responsive Data Selection (CRDS), a post-training data-selection principle that prioritizes examples with empirically demonstrated marginal utility from additional reasoning. On Qwen3-8B, SFT on CR examples recovers 45.3\% of held-out low-compute failures, compared with 40.6\% when training on already-solved examples. The advantage extends beyond the selected CR split: SFT-CR reaches 51.8\% overall accuracy on an independently sampled test distribution, with the gain concentrated on compute-responsive problems. CR training also shifts the compute--accuracy frontier across inference budgets from 512 to 4,096 tokens, outperforming matched non-CR training throughout and reaching 48.1\% recovery at the largest budget. The same pattern is supported across multiple data sources, remains visible under on-policy distillation, and extends to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct when CR sets are reconstructed separately for that model. Better test-time compute utilization can therefore be learned through post-training, with recoverable responses to additional reasoning providing a particularly informative signal for selecting training examples.

We first demonstrate that this direction generalizes across factual-conflict settings, including context formats, knowledge categories, and datasets, while consistently shifting behavior between parametric and contextual answers.     Dai Shi, Andi Han, Xiaoyu Li, Luke Thompson, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper develops a formal lattice framework for comparing hypotheses about representation convergence and analyzes how alignment criteria behave across models and training objectives. This directly advances representation geometry; its discussion of autoencoders and contrastive models does not substantively address composition, reasoning, or model systems.

    本文建立了一个形式化的格框架，用于比较有关表征收敛的假设，并分析对齐标准在不同模型和训练目标下的表现。这直接推进了表征几何研究；其中关于自编码器和对比模型的讨论，并未实质涉及组合、推理或模型系统。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) holds that increasingly capable models converge toward a common representation. However, recent studies have shown different views on aligning representations via their neighborhoods, spanning trees, and distances. We show that these views can differ because the alignment criteria behind them sit at different points of one lattice, and we formalize this explanation as the Lattice Representation Hypothesis (LRH). Under the LRH, the convergence claimed by the PRH is agreement at the top of the lattice, whereas its evidence comes from neighbor overlap, a criterion near the bottom. The Aristotelian Representation Hypothesis (ARH) restricts convergence to local neighborhoods because calibration keeps the growth of neighbor overlap with model size but largely removes that of centered kernel alignment. We show that this removal can come from calibrating a maximum over layers, so global convergence remains open. Back into Plato's Cave (BPC) infers coarse shared structure from the collapse of neighbor overlap on larger evaluation sets, whereas we trace it at least partly to a fixed number of neighbors covering shorter distances. We show that the spanning-tree overlap used by Structure over Geometry (SOG) mostly repeats one-nearest-neighbor overlap. The LRH also extends to independently trained models, whose training procedure and objective decide the criteria met reliably across runs. We prove this claim for the training procedure in a linear autoencoder and for the objective in a finite contrastive Gibbs model. Experiments on dozens of pretrained vision and language models and thousands of runs of both theoretical models support these conclusions. We hope this work paves the way toward a general theory of representation hypotheses, with a framework to analyze them and compare their evidence. Project page: https://eethanshi.github.io/LRH

    柏拉图式表征假设（PRH）认为，能力不断增强的模型会趋向一种共同表征。然而，近期研究通过邻域、生成树和距离来对齐表征，得出了不同观点。我们指出，这些观点之所以可能不同，是因为其背后的对齐标准位于同一个格的不同位置；我们将这一解释形式化为格表征假设（LRH）。按照 LRH，PRH 所主张的收敛是在格顶端达成一致，而其证据来自邻居重叠这一接近格底端的标准。亚里士多德式表征假设（ARH）将收敛限定在局部邻域，因为校准会保留邻居重叠随模型规模增大的趋势，却大幅消除中心化核对齐的这一趋势。我们表明，这种消除可能源于对跨层最大值进行校准，因此全局收敛仍是一个开放问题。Back into Plato's Cave（BPC）从较大评估集上的邻居重叠崩塌推断出粗粒度的共享结构；而我们发现，这至少部分是因为固定数量的邻居覆盖了更短的距离。我们表明，Structure over Geometry（SOG）使用的生成树重叠，大多只是重复了最近邻重叠。LRH 还扩展到独立训练的模型；这些模型能否在多次运行中可靠地满足相应标准，取决于其训练过程和目标函数。我们分别在线性自编码器中针对训练过程、在有限对比 Gibbs 模型中针对目标函数证明了这一主张。对数十个预训练视觉和语言模型以及上述两种理论模型的数千次运行开展的实验支持这些结论。我们希望这项工作能为表征假设的一般理论铺平道路，并提供一个用于分析表征假设及比较其证据的框架。项目页面：https://eethanshi.github.io/LRH

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    HiMeco diagnoses failures in embodied task execution, reflects across attempts, and consolidates reusable parameterized skills and strategies in memory, improving benchmark performance with frozen model parameters. This substantially advances agent memory and organization and supports multi-step planning, while its brain-inspired framing does not provide direct evidence about internal model mechanisms or representation geometry.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.

    中文

    视觉语言模型（VLM）在空间推理方面取得了显著进展，而自演化智能体通过从交互中学习，进一步将这些能力扩展到具身环境。然而，当前的自演化在具身空间任务中仍面临尤其严峻的挑战：任务决策复杂且涉及多个步骤，依据不完整的视觉证据很难判断执行失败的原因。失败可能源于感知错误、探索不足或规划不当，但仅靠执行反馈很少能揭示问题出在哪个环节。因此，单纯积累交互经验可能会强化无效策略。为此，我们提出 HiMeco，这是一种面向具身空间智能、受元认知监控和海马体记忆巩固启发的自演化智能体。HiMeco 通过海马体—元认知反思诊断感知—探索—规划（PEP）环节中的失败，随后比较不同执行尝试，提炼可复用策略和避免重复错误的指导。它还将交互程序抽象为参数化技能，并利用证据契约和基于执行的验证来决定是否保留和复用这些技能。这些策略和技能可指导后续交互，记忆仅在轮次之间更新，模型参数则保持冻结。HiMeco 在 ESI-Bench 上达到最先进的表现；在不进行演化的情况下，它还将 EmbSpatial-Bench 上的准确率提高了 3.94 个百分点。

    TreeFlex：智能体在自身搜索树中导航

    Dongzhuo Li, Fangzhou Cheng, Weiwei Li, Kevin Han, Haixu Ma, Zhongchang Sun, Ruiyi Li, Serena Li, Xiangjun Fan, Lizhu Zhang, Yuandong Tian

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    TreeFlex’s main contribution is a jointly trained agent that navigates a tree of its own intermediate states to manage context and improve task execution. Its adaptive search supports multi-step reasoning (4) and directly advances agent organization and memory use (5); branching alone offers only an incidental connection to compositional generalization (2), with no interpretability contribution (1).

    TreeFlex 的主要贡献是一个经过联合训练的智能体，它在自身中间状态构成的树中导航，以管理上下文并改善任务执行。其自适应搜索支持多步推理（4），并直接推动智能体组织与记忆使用的发展（5）；单凭分支机制与组合泛化只有附带关联（2），且没有可解释性方面的贡献（1）。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    A ReAct-style agent accumulates observations, intermediate results, and failed attempts in a single context. As this context grows, stale and off-path information consumes its limited capacity and obscures relevant evidence, making focused reasoning increasingly difficult. We introduce TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent's own policy decides where to search. The agent records each intermediate state, with a short summary, as a node in a search tree maintained by the harness. The policy is a single language model that acts in two roles. In the Reflection role, it has a global view of the tree through these summaries and picks a node to resume, together with an instruction. In the Execution role, the harness restores the path that led to that node, and the model carries out the instruction with the usual task tools until it saves a new node or proposes a solution, which Reflection then approves or sends back to another node. Through these choices, the policy decides whether to deepen the current line, branch from or revisit an earlier state, verify a proposal, or stop, without a fixed traversal order or a score for each node. We train navigation, task actions, checkpointing, and proposal review jointly with a tree-aware adaptation of GRPO, using task-level outcome rewards augmented by process rewards. After small-scale RL of a 4B model, with the same active-context limit for all methods, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy on a challenging deep-research benchmark, versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and its Pass@8 is about ten points higher than either. On SWE-bench Verified, with all three systems trained with RL from the same 9B model, TreeFlex resolves 54.9% of tasks, versus 43.3% for FoldAgent and 45.2% for its step-wise variant.

    中文

    ReAct 风格的智能体会在单一上下文中累积观察、中间结果和失败尝试。随着上下文增长，过时及偏离路径的信息会占用有限容量并遮蔽相关证据，使聚焦推理越来越困难。我们提出 TreeFlex，这是一个由智能体自身策略决定搜索位置的框架。智能体将每个中间状态连同简短摘要记录为由执行框架维护的搜索树中的一个节点。该策略由一个在两种角色间切换的语言模型承担。在反思角色中，模型通过这些摘要全局查看搜索树，并选择一个要恢复的节点，同时给出一条指令。在执行角色中，执行框架恢复通往该节点的路径，模型则使用常规任务工具执行指令，直到保存新节点或提出解决方案；随后，反思角色会批准该方案，或将其发回另一个节点。通过这些选择，策略决定是沿当前路径深入、从先前状态分支或返回先前状态、验证提议，还是停止，而无需固定的遍历顺序，也无需为每个节点评分。我们使用面向树结构的 GRPO 改进方法，联合训练导航、任务操作、检查点保存和方案审查，并以任务级结果奖励辅以过程奖励。对一个 4B 模型进行小规模 RL 训练后，在所有方法的活动上下文限制相同的条件下，TreeFlex 在具有挑战性的深度研究基准上达到 48.8% 的准确率，高于平面 ReAct 的 41.5% 和 FoldAgent 的 42.8%；其 Pass@8 也比两者分别高约十个百分点。在 SWE-bench Verified 上，三个系统均从同一个 9B 模型出发进行 RL 训练，TreeFlex 解决了 54.9% 的任务，而 FoldAgent 为 43.3%，其逐步变体为 45.2%。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Preference optimization ranks final answers and trajectory RL maximizes aggregate returns, yet neither credits the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. We introduce Lifted State Policy Optimization (LSPO), which establishes this finite, cost-adjusted transition as the primary unit of learning. Each textual answer is augmented with a learned continuous coordinate, forming a lifted state that an energy function evaluates and orders. A shaped reward drives energy descent net of edit and step costs, and an internalization loss absorbs selected low-energy answers into the direct generator. On Qwen3.5-27B, the resulting single-pass policy reaches 71.8% aggregate accuracy across mathematics, science, code, and logic benchmarks, matching test-time reflection at 71.9% with 28% lower latency and 25.8% fewer tokens. The pattern holds across dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, and matched controls confirm that transition credit and the lifted coordinate each contribute, as does answer internalization. Our code is available at https://github.com/Venomrko/lspo.

    偏好优化对最终答案排序，轨迹 RL 最大化总体回报，但两者都没有对将有缺陷的推理状态转变为更好状态的局部变化给予奖励。我们提出提升状态策略优化（LSPO），将这种有限且经过成本调整的转移确立为学习的基本单位。每个文本答案都附加一个学习得到的连续坐标，从而形成一个由能量函数评估和排序的提升状态。塑形奖励推动能量下降，同时扣除编辑和步骤成本；内化损失则将选定的低能量答案融入直接生成器。在 Qwen3.5-27B 上，由此得到的单次处理策略在数学、科学、代码和逻辑基准上的总体准确率达到 71.8%，与测试时反思的 71.9% 相当，同时延迟降低 28%，token 数减少 25.8%。这一趋势在稠密型和混合专家骨干网络上均成立；匹配对照实验确认，转移奖励、提升坐标以及答案内化各自都有贡献。代码见 https://github.com/Venomrko/lspo。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Tabular foundation models enable in-context learning by predicting unseen observations from a labeled support table without task-specific parameter updates. Despite recent advances, most existing approaches rely on dense architectures that apply the same transformations across features and datasets. We introduce OrionMoE-Small, a compact tabular foundation model that combines distribution-aware representations with dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts computation. Built on a dual-axis Transformer architecture, OrionMoE-Small selectively activates experts along the feature axis, with routing decisions informed by both individual feature representations and the broader dataset context. This design enables adaptive allocation of computation across heterogeneous tabular problems while retaining a shared computational pathway across tasks. OrionMoE-Small is pretrained entirely on synthetic classification tasks generated from a structured causal prior and performs downstream prediction without gradient-based adaptation. Experiments across multiple tabular benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance against substantially larger foundation models, with particularly strong results on small-context and high-dimensional datasets. Further analysis reveals favorable relative performance under class imbalance and highlights the importance of feature composition.

    Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling

    用于免训练推理时扩展的解耦边缘锐化

    Weixin Wang, Wei Deng, Anderson Schneider, Yuriy Nevmyvaka, Pan Xu, Andrew Bennett

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper develops inference-time sampling methods that preserve diverse reasoning paths while sharpening answers, directly advancing reasoning and problem-solving. Its path aggregation and SMC sampling have only limited compositional relevance and are system-level techniques rather than contributions to model internals or system architecture.

    本文开发了推理时采样方法，在锐化答案的同时保留多样的推理路径，直接推进了推理和问题求解。其路径聚合和 SMC 采样与组合能力只有有限关联，且属于系统层面的技术，并非对模型内部机制或系统架构的贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    We study how to improve LLM reasoning at inference time without updating model weights or using external reward models. Recent reward-free power-sampling methods define the sequence-level power target $\pi_\alpha(y\mid x)\propto p_0(y\mid x)^\alpha$, where $\alpha>1$, which increases the relative probability of completions that are already likely under the base model. Existing methods use Metropolis--Hastings or Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to approximately sample from this target. However, two challenges arise at different levels. At the target level, full-sequence sharpening can concentrate probability on a few exact reasoning--answer trajectories, suppressing alternative paths that support the same answer. At the sampler level, finite-particle SMC can suffer from path collapse when resampling repeatedly duplicates a few high-weight prefixes. To address these challenges, we propose Decoupled Marginal Sharpening (DMS), which separately controls how strongly the model favors particular reasoning paths and how strongly it favors final answers after aggregating support across those paths. At the target level, DMS first samples from a sharpened reasoning distribution, then marginalizes the model's answer probabilities over the resulting weighted reasoning population and sharpens the induced answer marginal. Separate exponents allow mild reasoning sharpening to encourage exploration of diverse paths, followed by stronger answer-marginal sharpening to concentrate probability on answers with greater aggregate support across those paths. At the sampler level, we develop Fully Adapted Annealed SMC, which combines an annealed sequence of power targets with locally fully adapted proposals and predictive ancestor resampling. Experiments on MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, and AIME24/25 across three base models show that DMS achieves the highest mean pass@1 among the compared methods in all tasks.

    中文

    我们研究如何在推理时提升 LLM 的推理能力，而无需更新模型权重或使用外部奖励模型。近期无奖励幂采样方法定义了序列级幂目标$\pi_\alpha(y\mid x)\propto p_0(y\mid x)^\alpha$其中$\alpha>1$，该目标提高了基础模型本已较可能生成的补全文本的相对概率。现有方法使用 Metropolis--Hastings 或序贯蒙特卡洛（SMC）近似地从该目标中采样。然而，不同层面上存在两个挑战。在目标层面，对完整序列进行锐化可能会将概率集中到少数精确的推理—答案轨迹上，从而压制那些支持相同答案的其他路径。在采样器层面，有限粒子的 SMC 可能发生路径坍缩：重采样会反复复制少数高权重前缀。为应对这些挑战，我们提出解耦边缘锐化（DMS），分别控制模型偏好特定推理路径的程度，以及模型在汇总不同路径上的支持后偏好最终答案的程度。在目标层面，DMS 首先从经过锐化的推理分布中采样，然后对所得加权推理集合中的模型答案概率求边缘分布，并锐化由此得到的答案边缘分布。分开的指数使推理锐化可以较为温和，以鼓励探索多样路径；随后再加强答案边缘分布的锐化，使概率集中到在这些路径上获得更强总体支持的答案。在采样器层面，我们开发了完全适配的退火 SMC，将一系列退火的幂目标与局部完全适配提议和预测式祖先重采样相结合。在 MATH500、GPQA-Diamond、HumanEval 和 AIME24/25 上使用三个基础模型进行的实验表明，在所有任务中，DMS 在所比较的方法里都取得了最高的平均 pass@1。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    VASPO combines privileged value estimates and self-teacher guidance in PPO to improve training of mathematical reasoning models, with gains across reasoning benchmarks.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. However, this supervision reflects local token preferences rather than the expected return of an unguided student continuation. Recent methods combine this signal with GRPO. They use GRPO for update directions and the teacher for signal scaling. However, we demonstrate a more effective integration within PPO. Specifically, we identify complementary positional dynamics: privileged information enhances a critic's value-prediction accuracy toward the response's end, whereas self-teacher guidance is strong initially, drops mid-generation, and rebounds finally. These insights motivate Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (VASPO), wherein a self-teacher and critic evaluate identical privileged information at student-generated prefixes. The critic computes token-level PPO advantages from predicted continuation returns, while the self-teacher modulates selected positive advantages via bounded probability ratios. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improves mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 and 1.81 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and OLMo3-7B variants, respectively, and achieves the highest mean accuracy among evaluated methods on Knights and Knaves.     Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting significantly enhances large language models' (LLMs) problem-solving capabilities, but still struggles with complex multi-hop questions, often falling into circular reasoning patterns or deviating from the logical path entirely.     Foundation models (FMs) have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of applications, from image classification to natural langurage processing, but pose significant challenges for deployment at edge. This has sparked growing interest in developing practical and efficient strategies for bringing foundation models to edge environments. In this work, we propose PRISM, a communication-efficient and compute-aware strategy for distributed Transformer inference on edge devices. Our method leverages a Segment Means representation to approximate intermediate output features, drastically reducing inter-device communication. Additionally, we restructure the self-attention mechanism to eliminate redundant computations caused by per-device Key/Value calculation in position-wise partitioning and design a partition-aware causal masking scheme tailored for autoregressive models. We evaluate PRISM on ViT, BERT, and GPT-2 across diverse datasets, namely CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, GLUE, and CBT. Our results demonstrate substantial reductions in communication overhead (up to 99.2% for BERT at compression rate CR = 128) and per-device computation (51.24% for BERT at the same setting), with only minor accuracy degradation.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Language models (LMs) are used for a diverse range of tasks, from question answering to writing fantastical stories. In order to reliably accomplish these tasks, LMs must be able to discern the modal category of a sentence (i.e., whether it describes something that is possible, impossible, completely nonsensical, etc.). However, recent studies have called into question the ability of LMs to categorize sentences according to modality (Michaelov et al., 2025; Kauf et al., 2023). In this work, we identify linear representations that discriminate between modal categories within a variety of LMs, or modal difference vectors. Analysis of modal difference vectors reveals that LMs have access to more reliable modal categorization judgments than previously reported. Furthermore, we find that modal difference vectors emerge in a consistent order as models become more competent (i.e., through training steps, layers, and parameter count). Notably, we find that modal difference vectors identified within LM activations can be used to model fine-grained human categorization behavior. This potentially provides a novel view into how human participants distinguish between modal categories, which we explore by correlating projections along modal difference vectors with human participants' ratings of interpretable features. In summary, we derive new insights into LM modal categorization using techniques from mechanistic interpretability, with the potential to inform our understanding of modal categorization in humans.

    ENGLISH

    Recent advances highlight Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) as a promising approach to enhancing LLM capabilities. However, it remains unclear whether the current practice of RLVR truly expands models' reasoning boundary or mainly amplifies high-reward outputs that base models already know. We introduce empirical support dynamics, a framework that quantifies how RLVR preserves, expands, and shrinks access to verified solutions. Applied across models, reasoning tasks, and training checkpoints, it matches verified successes question by question to reveal changes that aggregate accuracy can conceal. Across the evaluated model-level benchmark aggregates, \textit{the shrinkage of observed support outweighs its expansion}: more questions lose a verified success than gain one at the stated sampling budgets. These losses occur alongside gains in \texttt{pass@1}. Some RLVR models increase average token-level entropy while reducing final-answer entropy: their token choices become more uncertain on average even as their final answers become more concentrated. Together, these findings reveal an ``invisible leash'' in current RLVR practice: it can make existing successes more reliable while losing access to other verified solutions. Empirical support dynamics make this imbalance measurable and motivate exploration strategies that reach underrepresented solutions while retaining prior successes.

    Agents in a society can reuse each other's experience, but indiscriminate memory use increases processing cost and can reduce task success. We present SEDM (Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory), a framework that selects both what agents share and when recipients use it. On the sender side, SEDM admits memories through paired execution tests, ranks them by relevance and measured utility, and abstracts them for cross-domain reuse. On the recipient side, Calibrated Memory Gating (CMG) predicts success with and without memory in a single forward pass, learning from paired outcomes including ties. It injects memory only when the calibrated success gain outweighs a context-cost penalty. SEDM exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline on LoCoMo open-domain questions by 15.1 F1 points and outperforms G-Memory on FEVER and HotpotQA with 16-32% fewer prompt tokens. In a controlled HotpotQA study, CMG achieves success comparable to always using memory with 18% fewer agent input tokens. Within the full SEDM pipeline on LoCoMo, CMG outperforms both always-use and no-memory policies for two SEDM memories while using 19-31% fewer input tokens than always-use. These results show that selective use can recover value from shared memories that hurt performance when injected indiscriminately.

    Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown strong progress on scientific reasoning, yet two major bottlenecks remain. First, explicit retrieval fragments reasoning, imposing a hidden "tool tax" of extra tokens and steps. Second, multi-agent pipelines often dilute strong solutions by averaging across all candidates. We address these challenges with a unified framework that combines implicit retrieval and structured collaboration. At its foundation, a Monitor-based retrieval module operates at the token level, integrating external knowledge with minimal disruption to reasoning. On top of this substrate, Hierarchical Solution Refinement (HSR) iteratively designates each candidate as an anchor to be repaired by its peers, while Quality-Aware Iterative Reasoning (QAIR) adapts refinement to solution quality. On Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) Bio/Chem Gold, our framework achieves 48.3% accuracy - the highest reported to date, surpassing the strongest agent baseline by 13.4 points and leading frontier LLMs by up to 18.1 points, while simultaneously reducing token usage by 53.5% and agent steps by 43.7%. Results on SuperGPQA and TRQA confirm robustness across domains. Error analysis shows that reasoning failures and knowledge gaps co-occur in over 85% of cases, while diversity analysis reveals a clear dichotomy: retrieval tasks benefit from solution variety, whereas reasoning tasks favor consensus. Together, these findings demonstrate how implicit augmentation and structured refinement overcome the inefficiencies of explicit tool use and uniform aggregation. The code is available at https://github.com/tangxiangru/Eigen-1.

    Jason Jabbour, Dong-Ki Kim, Max Smith, Jay Patrikar, Radhika Ghosal, Youhui Wang, Ali Agha, Vijay Janapa Reddi, Shayegan Omidshafiei

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper analyzes why pruning harms VLA performance and safety, then proposes a weight-space correction that recovers capability while retaining sparsity. Spectral analysis offers some mechanistic insight, but the central contribution is a practical model-compression and recovery method, strongly relevant to systems.

    本文分析了剪枝损害 VLA 性能和安全性的原因，并提出一种权重空间校正方法，在保留稀疏性的同时恢复模型能力。谱分析提供了一些机制层面的见解，但其核心贡献是一种实用的模型压缩与恢复方法，与系统领域高度相关。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are a promising paradigm for field robotics, but their deployment is bottlenecked by strict edge SWaP-C constraints. Compression techniques such as quantization, distillation, and pruning are well-established for LLMs and VLMs. Pruning, however, remains particularly underexplored for VLA models. We surprisingly find that pruning VLA models yields drastic performance degradation and increased safety violations. Through spectral analysis, we identify structural properties of VLA weights that help explain this fragility. Based on this insight, we introduce GLUESTICK, a post-pruning recovery method that restores much of the original model's capability while preserving sparsity benefits. GLUESTICK computes a one-time corrective term by interpolating between the dense and pruned models in weight space. At inference, each pruned layer applies this correction to recover lost performance with minimal overhead. Our approach requires no additional training and is agnostic to the pruning algorithm. Across diverse VLA architectures and domains, GLUESTICK recovers up to 100% of the success rate and restores safety to near-dense levels, while saving up to 5 GB of memory and achieving up to 1.75x speedup. Additional material can be found at: https://gluestick-vla.github.io/

    Shuo Xing, Junyuan Hong, Yifan Wang, Runjin Chen, Zhenyu Zhang, Ananth Grama, Zhengzhong Tu, and Zhangyang Wang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    Controlled continual-pretraining experiments link junk-data exposure to declines in reasoning and other capabilities, identify skipped chains as a reasoning failure mode, and report persistent representational drift. The causal evidence and analysis substantially inform reasoning development and model representations, but the abstract does not study compositionality or system organization.

    受控的持续预训练实验将劣质数据暴露与推理等能力下降联系起来，识别出跳过推理链这一失败模式，并报告了持久的表示漂移。这些因果证据和分析对推理发展及模型表示具有重要意义，但摘要并未研究组合性或系统组织。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    We propose and test the LLM Brain Rot Hypothesis: continual exposure to junk web text induces lasting cognitive decline in large language models (LLMs). To unveil junk effects, we designed a novel controlled experiment on real Twitter/X corpora, by constructing junk and reverse-controlled datasets via two orthogonal operationalizations: M1 (engagement degree) and M2 (semantic quality), with matched token scale and training operations across conditions. Compared to the control group, continual pre-training of 4 LLMs on the junk dataset causes non-trivial declines (Hedges' g>0.3) on reasoning, long-context understanding, safety, and inflating "dark traits" (e.g., psychopathy, narcissism). The gradual mixtures of junk and control datasets also yield dose-response cognition decay: for example, under M1, ARC-Challenge with Chain-of-Thought drops 72.1 -> 57.2 and RULER-CWE 83.7 -> 52.3 as junk ratio rises from 0% to 100%. Error forensics reveal several key insights. First, we identify thought-skipping as the primary lesion in reasoning: models increasingly truncate or skip chains. Second, partial but incomplete healing is observed: scaling instruction tuning and clean continual pre-training improve the declined cognition, yet cannot restore baseline capability, suggesting persistent representational drift rather than format mismatch. Finally, we discover that the popularity, a non-semantic metric, of a tweet is a better indicator of the Brain Rot effect than the length in M1. Together, the results provide significant, multi-perspective evidence that social effects of data could be a causal driver of LLM capability decay in continual pre-training, thereby motivating routine "cognitive health checks" for deployed and evolving LLMs.

    While reinforcement learning agents can achieve superhuman performance in many complex tasks, they typically do not become more computationally efficient as they improve. In contrast, humans gradually require less cognitive effort as they become more proficient at a task. If agents could reason about their compute as they learn, could they similarly reduce their computation footprint? If they could, we could have more energy efficient agents or free up compute cycles for other processes like planning. In this paper, we experiment with showing agents the cost of their computation and giving them the ability to control when they use compute. We conduct our experiments on the Arcade Learning Environment, and our results demonstrate that with the same training compute budget, agents that reason about their compute perform better on 75% of games. Furthermore, these agents use three times less compute on average. We analyze individual games and show where agents gain these efficiencies.     We propose a novel cognitively-inspired prompting method to stabilize and interpret the physical simulation produced by autoregressive image generation models, called Chain-of-Time. Chain-of-Time involves generating a series of intermediate images during a simulation, and it is motivated by mental simulation in humans, as well as in-context reasoning in LLMs. Chain-of-Time is used at inference time, and requires no additional fine-tuning. We apply this method to synthetic and real-world domains, including 2-D graphics simulations and natural 3-D videos. These domains cover various physical dynamics, ranging from rigid-body rolling to harmonic oscillation and pulley systems. We found that Chain-of-Time simulation stabilizes the physics simulated by the state-of-the-art image generation models. Beyond examining performance, we also analyzed the specific states of the world simulated by an image model at each time step, which sheds light on the dynamics underlying these simulations. This analysis reveals insights that are hidden from traditional evaluations of physical reasoning, highlighting cases where image generation models can simulate physical properties such as velocity, gravity, oscillations, and pulley systems. Like humans, image generation models are able to accurately predict future world states over short time periods. By providing a mechanism analogous to working memory, Chain-of-Time enables a model to stitch together a series of short-term predictions into an accurate long-term simulation.

Existing methods for automated reward optimization search with a fixed proposer which never learns from its costly trials. An outer-loop proposer composes a reward from task primitives, and an inner policy trains with this reward. The proposer itself learns by policy gradient from the validation performance of the inner policy. Thus, DERL utilizes past-trial feedback to shape its reward-proposal distribution, an empirical meta-gradient of task success. We validate DERL on embodied (ALFWorld), scientific (ScienceWorld), and mathematical (GSM8K, MATH) reasoning. On multi-turn agent benchmarks, DERL outperforms strong baselines, significantly on out-of-distribution tasks. In mathematics, DERL improves on the outcome reward where directly added primitives hurt. Further analyses under matched compute show that our proposer effectively captures the meta-gradient to discover useful reward signals.

    Large Language Models (LLMs) deployed in practical and safety-critical settings are increasingly susceptible to bit-flip faults caused by hardware degradation, cosmic radiation, or deliberate fault-injection attacks such as Rowhammer. These faults silently corrupt internal parameters and can lead to unpredictable or dangerous model behavior. Localizing these corruptions is essential: without identifying the affected region, it is impossible to diagnose the source of degradation, apply targeted corrective measures, or restore model functionality without resorting to costly fine-tuning or full retraining. This work introduces BitFlipScope, a scalable, software-based framework for identifying fault-affected regions within transformer architectures under two deployment scenarios. When a clean reference model is available, BitFlipScope performs differential analysis of outputs, hidden states, and internal activations for detecting anomalous behavior indicative of corruption to pinpoint or localize faults. When no reference model exists, it uses residual-path perturbation and loss-sensitivity profiling to infer the fault-impacted region directly from the corrupted model. In both settings, the framework not only enables effective fault diagnosis but also supports lightweight performance recovery without fine-tuning, offering a practical path to restoring corrupted models. Together, these capabilities make BitFlipScope an important step toward trustworthy, fault-resilient LLM deployment in hardware-prone and adversarial environments.

    ENGLISH

    Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in finance-oriented question answering, yet their evaluation on professional quantitative workflows remains fragmented and often stops at factual or document-grounded QA. We introduce QuantEval, a benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can complete the compute--implement--validate loop required in quantitative finance. QuantEval contains 1,575 expert-validated instances across three complementary dimensions: (i) knowledge-based QA, (ii) quantitative mathematical reasoning, and (iii) quantitative strategy coding. The coding task is evaluated with a deterministic CTA-style backtesting framework that executes model-generated strategies and compares risk--return metrics against expert references, moving beyond syntax or template matching. We evaluate 13 open-source and proprietary LLMs, report prompt and reliability analyses, and observe substantial gaps relative to human experts, especially in multi-step reasoning and framework-constrained coding. We further conduct supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning experiments on domain-aligned data, showing that training can improve quantitative reasoning while also exposing trade-offs in factual recall. QuantEval releases the dataset, evaluation scripts, and full backtesting configuration to support reproducible research on LLMs for quantitative finance.

    LB-MCTS combines tree-structured search, algorithm-specific surrogates, and path-aware LLM memory, with adaptive proposal allocation for structured AutoML optimization.     ENGLISH

    To lower the expertise barrier in machine learning, the AutoML community has focused on the CASH problem, which jointly automates algorithm selection and hyperparameter tuning. While traditional methods like Bayesian Optimization (BO) struggle with cold-start issues, Large Language Models (LLMs) can mitigate these through semantic priors. However, existing LLM-based optimizers generalize poorly to high-dimensional, structured CASH spaces. CASH requires coordinated exploration and exploitation both across candidate algorithms and within their algorithm-specific hyperparameter spaces. Yet existing approaches often rely on flat optimization histories that mix observations across algorithms and obscure configuration-refinement trajectories. In this paper, we propose LB-MCTS, a trajectory-structured optimization framework that uses a Monte Carlo Tree Search tree as a shared state for algorithm selection, hyperparameter refinement, and BO-LLM proposer synergy. Within this shared state, BO provides algorithm-specific surrogate modeling for quantitative search, while the LLM exploits path-aware selective memory to generate semantic proposals and reflections. As the surrogate model improves, a reliability-aware proposer policy adaptively shifts from LLM-driven to BO-driven proposals within a unified search trajectory. Experiments on 104 AMLB datasets demonstrate that LB-MCTS consistently outperforms BO-based, LLM-based, and hybrid baselines. Code: https://github.com/PKU-DAIR/open-box.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    The deployment of coding agents in privacy-sensitive and resource-constrained environments drives the demand for capable open-weight Small Language Models (SLMs). However, they suffer from a fundamental capability gap: unlike frontier large models, they lack the inference-time strong generalization to handle complicated, unfamiliar codebases. We identify that the prevailing Task-Centric Learning (TCL) approach, which scales exposure across disparate repositories, fails to address this limitation. In response, we propose Repository-Centric Learning (RCL), a shift that prioritizes vertical, single-repository depth over horizontal, single-task breadth for SLM training. To accomplish this depth, we design a four-unit Repository-Centric Experience, transforming static codebases into interactive learning signals, to train SWE-Spot-4B, a family of highly compact models built as repo-specialized experts. Under controlled comparisons with the same teacher and data budget, RCL consistently outperforms TCL across tasks, teachers, model scales, and programming languages. On seven target repositories, SWE-Spot-4B experts match or exceed existing open-weight models up to $8\times$ larger (e.g., CWM by Meta, Qwen3-Coder-30B) and surpass or match efficiency-focused commercial models (e.g., GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-5-nano) across multiple SWE tasks. Further analysis reveals that RCL yields higher training and inference efficiency, deep knowledge acquisition, and can scale to repository-cluster experts. Our work emphasizes that for building efficient intelligence, repository mastery is a distinct, necessary, and practical dimension that complements general coding capability.

    Intrinsic Motivation (IM) aims to train agents without external rewards, enabling useful behavior to emerge from the agent's interaction with its environment alone. However, the dominant IM approaches rely on information-theoretic quantities with designer-chosen variables, introducing bias and lacking a principled connection to dynamics or optimal control (OC). We introduce Controllable Information Production (CIP), a novel IM method explicitly grounded in dynamical systems and OC. CIP measures the rate at which an agent produces information, capturing controllable complexity without external knowledge or bias. CIP unifies IM and OC into a single framework, formalizing physical intelligence as the control of information production. It further reveals connections between the structure of the value function and Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy. CIP consistently outperforms prior IM methods on standard benchmarks in robot learning and solves tasks they fail on, including humanoid self-righting. These results support an organizing principle: that physical intelligence emerges from driving systems toward the edge of controllable chaos.

    In agentic search, an LLM agent searches the web, reads the pages it finds, and decides what to look for next before returning an answer. But can we trust an answer simply because the agent returns it? Often not, and even a correct answer can be a lucky guess: on questions with several constraints, we find that agents conclude the task is complete while a constraint remains unverified in up to 48% of their correct answers. We call this illusory completion. To see how it arises, we introduce the Epistemic Ledger, which tracks at every turn what the retrieved pages establish about each constraint and what the agent claims. Across 13 agents, from 7B RL-trained models to frontier LLMs, training and scale raise accuracy but change the pattern of verification failures rather than eliminating them: constraints may be left unchecked, assumed without support, or retained despite refuting evidence. To measure what agents lose without tracking their constraints, we show them each constraint's state, approximated by LiveLedger, a lightweight 4B tracker. Agents then answer 4.4-16.1 points more questions correctly, suggesting that on their own, they may not track what they have verified and what remains.

    Mehryar Mohri

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper introduces a recurrent, automata-based Transformer architecture with theoretical expressive-power results and improved length generalization on algorithmic tasks. This advances sequential computation and systematic generalization, while internal representation mechanisms are not a focus.

    该论文提出了一种基于自动机的递归 Transformer 架构，给出了关于表达能力的理论结果，并提升了算法任务上的长度泛化能力。这推进了序列计算和系统性泛化，但没有重点研究内部表征机制。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Standard Transformers excel at semantic modeling but struggle with rigid sequential logic and state tracking. Theoretical work establishes that self-attention is limited to $\AC^0$ (under hard attention) or $\TC^0$ (under soft attention), complexity classes that often fail to support robust length generalization on sequential problems without intermediate chain-of-thought \citep{hahn2020theoretical, hao2022formal, merrill2022saturated}. In this work, we introduce \emph{Rational Transductors}, a dual-stream architecture that augments the Transformer with a matrix-valued recurrence derived from Weighted Finite Automata (WFA). By injecting rational state information into the attention mechanism via a \emph{Deep Rational Injection} scheme, our framework strictly generalizes the expressive power of Transformers to capture all Regular Languages, $\NC^1$-complete languages (such as the word problem of $S_5$), and fundamental separations like Parity and Modular Counting, while preserving $O(\log T)$ parallel training efficiency. We ground the architecture in a rigorous learning theory: we prove that \emph{Random Rational Features} act as a universal basis for sequential dependencies, justifying our initialization strategy, while establishing that the \emph{Differentiable Rational Feature} regime is necessary to close the representational compactness gap. Theoretical analysis and empirical results demonstrate that Rational Transductors solve the ``Regular Gap,'' enabling robust length generalization on algorithmic tasks where standard Transformers fail, without the sequential computational bottlenecks of traditional RNNs.

    Scaling network depth has been a central driver behind the success of modern foundation models, yet recent investigations suggest that deep layers are often underutilized. This paper revisits the default mechanism for deepening neural networks, namely residual connections, from an optimization perspective. Rigorous analysis proves that the layout of residual connections can fundamentally shape convergence behavior, and even induces an exponential gap in convergence rates. Prompted by this insight, we introduce adaptive neural connection reassignment (ANCRe), a principled and lightweight framework that parameterizes and learns residual connectivities from the data. ANCRe adaptively reassigns residual connections with negligible computational and memory overhead ($<1\%$), while enabling more effective utilization of network depth.     几何对齐不等于功能等价：语音—文本模态差距的逐层分析

    Ming-Hao Hsu, Xiaohai Tian, Jun Zhang, Lu Lu, Yuxuan Wang, Zhizheng Wu

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The study tests whether speech-text representational alignment predicts equivalent answers, and uses an attention intervention to identify a causal effect on answer-code separation. This is a substantial contribution to representation geometry and model mechanisms; its focus on answer formation is relevant to reasoning, but does not directly develop reasoning methods or capabilities.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    End-to-end speech large language models (LLMs) often answer the same question less accurately from speech than from text, even when the spoken content matches the text prompt. Existing analyses study this modality gap through the geometry of representations and measure how closely speech representations align with text. Geometric alignment gives the gap a measurable form, but it does not show whether the model uses aligned representations in the same way. This work connects representation geometry with answer formation and asks whether geometric alignment implies functional equivalence. We compare cross-layer Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) with layer-wise answer margins for four open-weight speech LLMs on SpeechMMLU and VoiceBench BBH. In Qwen2.5-Omni and MiniCPM-o, speech and text representations align in middle layers while their late-layer answer margins still differ, so mid-layer alignment does not imply functional equivalence. Qwen2-Audio instead shows weak alignment, which indicates a different failure mode. An attention intervention at fixed input and token count identifies a causal effect of late attention allocation on answer-code separation, a quantity distinct from answer correctness. Compressing the speech signal or its token sequence repairs a subset of the errors that occur only with speech.

    As web agents close the gap with humans on benchmarks, one question arises: Do today's agents perform just as well on tomorrow's web? We introduce TimeWarp, a benchmark that emulates the evolving web. TimeWarp consists of three web environments, each with six UI versions spanning UI design, frontend code, and workflows from different eras of the internet. We pair TimeWarp with a set of complex, realistic tasks covering different forms of web navigation. Our experiments reveal that vision-based agents are vulnerable to changes, while text-based agents become brittle once fine-tuned on a single version. To address this, we propose TimeTraj, a new annotation method that uses plan distillation to collect trajectories across multiple versions. By training agents on teacher rollouts using our BC-variant, we achieve substantial performance gains: 20.4% to 37.7% for Qwen-3 4B and 0% to 27.0% for Llama-3.1 8B models. Our work helps study generalization across web designs and opens a new paradigm for collecting plans rather than trajectories to improve the robustness of web agents.

    NePPO: Near-Potential Policy Optimization for General-Sum Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

    NePPO：用于一般和式多智能体强化学习的近似势函数策略优化

    Addison Kalanther, Sanika Bharvirkar, Shankar Sastry, Chinmay Maheshwari

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    NePPO introduces an objective and zeroth-order optimization pipeline for approximate Nash equilibria in mixed cooperative–competitive multi-agent settings. This substantially advances multi-agent learning systems and has partial relevance to strategic problem-solving, but the abstract does not address internal representations or compositional generalization.

    NePPO 为混合合作—竞争的多智能体场景引入了用于求取近似纳什均衡的目标函数和零阶优化流程。这显著推进了多智能体学习系统，并与策略性问题求解有部分关联，但摘要未涉及内部表征或组合泛化。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is increasingly used to design learning-enabled agents that interact in shared environments. However, training MARL algorithms in general-sum games remains challenging: learning dynamics can become unstable, and convergence guarantees typically hold only in restricted settings such as two-player zero-sum or fully cooperative games. Moreover, when agents have heterogeneous and potentially conflicting preferences, it is unclear what system-level objective should guide learning. In this paper, we propose a new MARL pipeline called Near-Potential Policy Optimization (NePPO) for computing approximate Nash equilibria in mixed cooperative--competitive environments. The core idea is to learn a player-independent potential function such that the Nash equilibrium of a cooperative game with this potential as the common utility approximates a Nash equilibrium of the original game. To this end, we introduce a novel MARL objective such that minimizing this objective yields the best possible potential function candidate and consequently an approximate Nash equilibrium of the original game. We develop an algorithmic pipeline that minimizes this objective using zeroth-order gradient descent and returns an approximate Nash equilibrium policy. We empirically show the superior performance of this approach compared to popular baselines such as IPPO and MAPPO.

    多智能体强化学习（MARL）日益用于设计能够在共享环境中交互的学习型智能体。然而，在一般和博弈中训练 MARL 算法仍面临挑战：学习动态可能变得不稳定，而收敛保证通常只适用于有限的设置，例如双人零和博弈或完全合作博弈。此外，当智能体具有异质且可能相互冲突的偏好时，尚不清楚应以何种系统级目标来引导学习。本文提出一种新的 MARL 流程，称为近似势函数策略优化（NePPO），用于在混合合作—竞争环境中计算近似纳什均衡。其核心思想是学习一个与玩家无关的势函数，使得在以该势函数为共同效用的合作博弈中得到的纳什均衡，能够近似原博弈的纳什均衡。为此，我们引入一种新的 MARL 目标，最小化该目标即可得到尽可能好的势函数候选，进而得到原博弈的近似纳什均衡。我们开发了一套使用零阶梯度下降来最小化该目标并返回近似纳什均衡策略的算法流程。实验证明，与 IPPO 和 MAPPO 等常用基线相比，该方法表现更优。

    The Reasoning Trap -- Logical Reasoning as a Mechanistic Pathway to Situational Awareness

    推理陷阱——逻辑推理作为通向情境意识的机制路径

    Subramanyam Sahoo, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Divya Chaudhary

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper maps logical reasoning capabilities to proposed pathways toward situational awareness and offers a benchmark and safeguards; its main contribution is an argument and framework about reasoning’s consequences.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Situational awareness, the capacity of an AI system to recognize its own nature, understand its training and deployment context, and reason strategically about its circumstances, is widely considered among the most dangerous emergent capabilities in advanced AI systems. Separately, a growing research effort seeks to improve the logical reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) across deduction, induction, and abduction. In this paper, we argue that these two research trajectories are on a collision course. We introduce the RAISE framework (Reasoning Advancing Into Self Examination), which identifies three mechanistic pathways through which improvements in logical reasoning enable progressively deeper levels of situational awareness: deductive self inference, inductive context recognition, and abductive self modeling. We formalize each pathway, construct an escalation ladder from basic self recognition to strategic deception, and demonstrate that every major research topic in LLM logical reasoning maps directly onto a specific amplifier of situational awareness. We further analyze why current safety measures are insufficient to prevent this escalation. We conclude by proposing concrete safeguards, including a "Mirror Test" benchmark and a Reasoning Safety Parity Principle, and pose an uncomfortable but necessary question to the logical reasoning community about its responsibility in this trajectory.

    情境意识是指 AI 系统识别自身本质、理解其训练和部署环境，并根据自身处境进行策略性推理的能力，被广泛认为是先进 AI 系统中最危险的涌现能力之一。与此同时，越来越多的研究致力于提升大语言模型（LLM）在演绎、归纳和溯因方面的逻辑推理能力。本文认为，这两条研究路线正走向碰撞。我们提出 RAISE 框架（推理迈向自我审视），指出逻辑推理能力的提升会通过三条机制路径促成逐渐深入的情境意识：演绎式自我推断、归纳式情境识别和溯因式自我建模。我们将每条路径形式化，构建一条从基本自我识别到策略性欺骗的升级阶梯，并展示 LLM 逻辑推理领域的每个主要研究主题都直接对应情境意识的某个特定增强因素。我们还分析了当前安全措施为何不足以防止这种升级。最后，我们提出具体的防护措施，包括“镜像测试”基准和推理安全均衡原则，并向逻辑推理研究群体提出一个令人不安却不可回避的问题：他们对这一发展轨迹负有何种责任。

    本文研究了 Transformer 的损失景观、参数稳定性，以及注意力与蛋白质接触图之间的关系，为模型表征和行为提供了机制层面的证据。蛋白质预测是其应用背景，而采样和注意力本身并不能构成对组合能力、推理或系统的贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Using a statistical mechanics framework, we investigate the parameter space of transformer models trained on protein sequence data. We sample the loss landscape at varying temperatures using Langevin dynamics to characterize the low-loss manifold, and to understand the mechanisms underlying transformers' superior performance in protein structure prediction. We find that, at variance with networks not based on the attention mechanism, the lack of a first--order--like transition in the loss of the transformer produces a range of intermediate temperatures with good learning properties; this is true both for synthetic and natural protein sequences. We also show that the parameters of most layers are highly conserved at these temperatures if the dimension of the embedding is optimal, and we provide an operative way to find this dimension. Additionally, we show that the attention matrix is more predictive of the contact maps of the protein at higher temperatures and for higher dimensions of the embedding than those optimal for learning. Finally, we showed that the models sampled at intermediate temperatures can predict the free-energy variation upon mutation, better than models obtained through standard optimization techniques.

    我们使用统计力学框架，研究在蛋白质序列数据上训练的 Transformer 模型的参数空间。我们使用朗之万动力学在不同温度下对损失景观进行采样，以刻画低损失流形，并理解 Transformer 在蛋白质结构预测中表现出色的机制。我们发现，与不基于注意力机制的网络不同，Transformer 的损失中缺乏类似一阶相变的转变，因此存在一段具有良好学习性质的中间温度范围；这对合成和天然蛋白质序列都成立。我们还表明，如果嵌入维度达到最优，大多数层的参数在这些温度下都高度稳定，并提供了一种实用的方法来寻找该维度。此外，我们表明，与最适合学习的温度相比，在更高温度下，以及在高于学习最优值的嵌入维度下，注意力矩阵对蛋白质接触图的预测能力更强。最后，我们表明，在中间温度下采样的模型预测突变引起的自由能变化的能力优于通过标准优化技术获得的模型。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    AdaptFuse externalizes Bayesian updating to a symbolic module and combines it with LLM predictions to accumulate evidence across interactions, improving sequential inference without fine-tuning. This is a substantial algorithmic contribution to reasoning and a partial contribution to systems through externalized computation and persistent preference state; recommendation applications alone do not support higher scores in the other directions.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLMs) struggle to accumulate evidence across multiple rounds of user interactions, failing to update their beliefs in a manner consistent with Bayesian inference. Existing solutions require fine-tuning on sensitive user interaction data, limiting their applicability in privacy-conscious settings. We propose \textsc{AdaptFuse}, a training-free framework that externalizes probabilistic computation entirely from the LLM, where a symbolic module maintains a Bayesian posterior over a discrete hypothesis set, while a frozen LLM contributes semantic reasoning via multi-sample Dirichlet aggregation. The two signals are combined through entropy-adaptive fusion, which automatically weights each source by its predictive confidence, shifting reliance from the LLM to the symbolic posterior as evidence accumulates. We evaluate across three domains: flight recommendation, hotel recommendation, and web shopping; on Gemma~2 9B, Llama~3 8B, and Qwen~2.5 7B. \textsc{AdaptFuse} consistently outperforms both prompting baselines and fine-tuned Bayesian Teaching models on all tasks, with accuracy improving monotonically over interaction rounds. These results demonstrate that principled inference-time algorithms can substitute for fine-tuning in personalized recommendation, without storing or training on sensitive user data.

    大型语言模型（LLM）难以在多轮用户交互中累积证据，无法以符合贝叶斯推断的方式更新其信念。现有解决方案需要使用敏感的用户交互数据进行微调，因此在注重隐私的场景中适用性有限。我们提出 \textsc{AdaptFuse}，一种免训练框架，将概率计算完全外置于 LLM：符号模块在离散假设集上维护贝叶斯后验，而冻结的 LLM 则通过多样本狄利克雷聚合提供语义推理。两种信号通过熵自适应融合相结合，该方法根据各自的预测置信度自动赋予权重；随着证据累积，系统会逐渐从依赖 LLM 转向依赖符号后验。我们在三个领域进行评估：航班推荐、酒店推荐和网络购物；使用的模型包括 Gemma~2 9B、Llama~3 8B 和 Qwen~2.5 7B。在所有任务上，\textsc{AdaptFuse} 的表现始终优于提示基线和经过微调的 Bayesian Teaching 模型，且准确率随交互轮数单调提升。这些结果表明，在个性化推荐中，有原则的推理时算法可以替代微调，无需存储敏感用户数据或使用这些数据进行训练。
