    ENGLISH

    Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two backbones, training improves AutomationBench task pass rates by 4.00-4.50 percentage points, JobBench weighted scores by 3.20-6.64 points, and Harvey LAB criterion pass rates by 3.89-4.16 percentage points. These results demonstrate the training utility of the synthesized experience across external task environments.

    Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves reasoning in language models, but scalar outcomes provide coarse supervision over response trajectories. We introduce Function-Space Policy Optimization (FSPO), a single-policy framework that combines current privileged adaptation with function-space temporal consolidation. FSPO stores sparse historical next-token distributions as fixed temporal targets, providing temporal separation without maintaining a persistent teacher model. It further introduces privileged disagreement correction to explicitly suppress locally overvalued actions, reliability-adaptive grounding that strengthens reference supervision when self-generated evidence repeatedly fails, and quality and coverage-aware temporal memory that retains verified behaviors and improves privileged demonstrations.     Large language models are increasingly trained as multi-turn agents that interact with external tools. However, outcome-only reinforcement learning can produce a form of misguided reinforcement: even on successful trajectories, undesirable local behaviors may receive positive token-level advantages and be favored by the policy update. To address this issue, we propose Confidence-Guided Credit Correction (C$^3$), a plug-in method for local credit correction. C$^3$ identifies spans corresponding to undesirable behaviors and selectively corrects positive credit after advantage estimation, with the correction strength adaptively controlled by the behavior policy's confidence in the corresponding behavior, while leaving the task reward and original credit estimation unchanged. Across multiple multi-turn benchmarks, C$^3$ improves performance under both {critic-based and critic-free reinforcement learning methods}. Injecting the same behavioral signals as turn-level or outcome rewards does not consistently improve performance. Our results show that local credit correction provides an effective form of process supervision for outcome-driven RL.

    Multi-agent systems allow language models to solve tasks collaboratively by sharing complementary information. These systems typically communicate through text, while recent approaches also explore exchanging internal model states. However, sharing these states across architectures often requires learned translators or assumptions about model compatibility. We introduce SYNC (Symbol-Indexed Neural Communication), a word-indexed interface that connects heterogeneous models without fine-tuning or a learned translator. From descriptions only it can see, the sender selects words from a shared list and sends their indices for each object, without seeing the questions. The receiver writes the described facts into its hidden states using its own word directions, vectors fitted once from its activations. We test selective use by swapping one attribute between two objects and requiring correct answers about both changed and unchanged attributes before and after the swap, four answers in total. We choose an early write layer on four development receivers and then fix it. With three different senders and nine newer receivers from five families, four-answer success on new scenes reaches 72.0-98.3%, up to 96 percentage points above middle-layer writing, and the two largest receivers match plain text. A task-free probe predicted in advance which depths each new receiver can use (45 of 45 cases). Without retuning, messages listing every fact keep 89.6-100% success under new layouts, and sender messages reach 23.9-64.0% on a landmark task with multi-token symbols, below text but from 0% without a message. These results show that shared word indices and receiver-local directions can support selective fact use across model families without additional training.

    RuleTrek 提供了一个多领域基准和一套流程，通过逐步组合特定规则的场景来评估智能体的规则识别与演绎能力。它重点关注组合泛化和推理评估；交互式工作区使智能体系统与该工作相关，但摘要没有提出系统机制。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLMs) increasingly tackle complex real-world tasks in specialized domains. However, identifying and correctly applying domain-specific rules remains challenging when scenario information is distributed across multiple files. Existing rule-reasoning benchmarks typically represent scenarios using only a few factual statements, simplifying the identification and application of relevant rules. To address this gap, this paper introduces \textbf{RuleTrek}, a multi-domain benchmark for agentic rule reasoning in complex scenarios. Its rule-grounded construction pipeline extracts structured rule graphs, generates and incrementally composes rule-specific sub-scenarios while ensuring consistency and solvability. To systematically evaluate agentic rule reasoning in complex scenarios, RuleTrek assesses three capabilities in interactive workspaces: Rule Identification (RI), Rule Deduction (RD), and End-to-End Rule Reasoning (E2E). Experiments on 11 frontier LLMs show that the highest RI and RD scores are only 62.47\% and 60.43\%, respectively, while E2E scores range from 26.97\% to 55.29\%. These results demonstrate that current LLM agents face substantial challenges in rule reasoning over complex scenarios. We make our code and dataset publicly available at \href{https://github.com/yuan247/RuleTrek}{RuleTrek}.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLMs) increasingly help users arrange appointments, plan journeys, and allocate limited resources. These tasks require models to satisfy constraints on time, cost, capacity, and order, or determine that no feasible solution exists. Bangla is the world's seventh most widely spoken language, and existing benchmarks cover many language and reasoning tasks. However, benchmarks for evaluating planning and decision-making in Bangla under explicit constraints remain lacking. We introduce BANGLAPLAN, a benchmark of 1,000 problems across ten task families grounded in everyday life and institutions in Bangladesh. It includes feasible and infeasible problems in four language registers: everyday, formal, colloquial, and Bangla--English mixed. Answers cover eight structured types, including schedules, routes, allocations, and ordered steps, in a common JSON format. We construct the benchmark through language-model-assisted drafting and independent human validation. We evaluate 11 open-weight and proprietary model configurations using exact match, separately reporting feasible-case accuracy, infeasibility detection, and format errors. We find a large performance gap: GPT-6.1 Sol achieves 98.7% accuracy and Qwen3.5-27B with thinking reaches 80.3%, while direct-answer configurations score at most 30.9%. Seven of eleven configurations perform below the always-``infeasible'' baseline. Our findings also suggest that harder problems primarily reduce plan-construction accuracy, while infeasibility detection remains more robust. BANGLAPLAN provides a reproducible basis for evaluating planning and decision-making in Bangla. BANGLAPLAN is available at: https://github.com/mrayhanulmasud/banglaplan.

    ENGLISH

    Multi-session agents can switch between LLMs to balance performance and inference cost. Such switches require transferring a history for continuity, yet their effects on the recipient remain underexplored. Through controlled experiments with multi-session tasks, we uncover behavior transfer: recipients tend to adopt reasoning and action patterns from the models that generated their histories. This effect is most evident with raw-history transfer but is substantially reduced by summarization. Based on these findings, we propose Direction- and Authorship-aware Summarization of History (DASH) that preserves stronger-model behavior while minimizing weak-to-strong transfer via summarization. Experiments with repeated swaps show that DASH outperforms raw-history transfer and naive summarization baselines. These results suggest that effective multi-model orchestration requires considering not only which model to use, but also which behavioral patterns to carry forward.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Goal misgeneralization is a common failure mode in which an agent behaves competently out of distribution but does not pursue the intended goal. However, we still have a weak understanding of what happens to the intended goal in misgeneralizing agents. Across three Procgen environments and five robot tasks, we find three distinct forms of policy-goal misalignment: (1) functional target substitution, where behavior follows an alternative goal, (2) a policy shortcut, where behavior follows a learned action strategy, and (3) cue competition between intended and proxy goal cues. We distinguish these regimes by tracing where goal information remains available internally, how strongly it influences the policy, and what role it plays in action selection, and find that the goal is lost at different depths. Where the goal reaches the decision, as in cue competition, steering redirects the policy to the goal's location, raising intended-goal reach from 16.0% to 95.3%. Where it reaches the policy but not the decision, only new downstream wiring recovers goal reach, from 31.6% to 84.3% in the environment with the action shortcut. Where it is inert, neither works. Our results show that goal misgeneralization is not a single failure of goal representation, but distinct failures of policy alignment at different depths, tightly connected to which recovery works.

We ask whether this trace can be exposed as a generative signal without task-specific guidance. We introduce the Discriminative Score Function (DSF), which extracts an image-space generative field from the loss-gradient geometry of a pretrained discriminative model. We apply DSF to diverse pretrained discriminative models, including ResNet classifiers, DETR detectors, and DINOv2 ViT encoders. DSF generates unconditional images from noise and supports conditional guidance, editing, inpainting, and explanation through the same field. Even when a correct answer is retrieved, its associated evidence and reasoning path may fail to support the relation composition required by the question. We term this disconnect between answer reachability and evidential validity the reachable-but-invalid problem. We present ReSemReason, which shares a question-induced distribution over typed, directed relation schemas between candidate discovery and evidence selection. A separate absolute-support score complements normalized attention when all retrieved paths are weak.     Medical prescribing errors for multimorbid patients, who require complex drug regimens, are a major patient safety concern. To address this coordination challenge, we introduce PRISMATIC, a multi-agent architecture where specialized agents, each representing a workflow role, collaboratively generate and refine treatment plans.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Reinforcement learning (RL) holds the promise of learning a policy that can outperform what is shown in the data. However, in practice, such systems suffer from instability and hyperparameter sensitivity. In contrast, supervised learning provides a stable and scalable training objective, but is fundamentally limited by the quality of the demonstrated behavior. In this paper, we ask whether we can perform policy optimization with something as simple and stable as supervised learning but as performant as RL. Unfortunately, naively training the policy with supervised learning and conditioning on future rewards or advantages typically underperform dedicated RL methods. We introduce a new policy extraction method, Advantage Guidance, that retains the simple supervised learning structure with advantage conditioning while outperforming prior RL methods through effective conditional training and contrastive diffusion guidance during sampling. We show that Advantage Guidance can significantly improve a model's ability to respond to conditional advantage signals, and the contrastive guidance during sampling can use the learned advantage-conditioned policy to target the KL-regularized optimal policy.     Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. We introduce a paradigm that decouples a persistent, updatable abstract state from the visual state. The abstract state keeps track of the entities' changes as the world evolves, and is used to condition the visual state, which represents the current view. We propose StateCraft, a novel architecture that pairs a language model with a video diffusion model to evolve the dynamic world. We evaluate our approach on generative interfaces, which pose a substantial challenge because a single action may change parts of the state that are not currently visible. To support training and evaluation, we develop a data collection pipeline that produces informative, densely annotated trajectories at scale without human or agent supervision, together with a benchmark measuring generation quality, memory, and controllability. On this benchmark, our approach improves surpasses the state-of-the-art baselines. We demonstrate that StateCraft maintains high self-consistency and strong generation quality over long trajectories. Because the abstract state is explicit, it can be edited directly, and generation follows edits to states never observed in the data. Finally, a proof-of-concept 3D experiment, in which actions change the illumination of an unobserved room, shows that the paradigm can also be applied to spatial environments. However, early predictive accessibility alone does not establish whether later layers are dispensable for every input, and aggregate accuracy can obscure which inputs benefit from additional computation. We study all 24 in-context-learning layers of TabPFN-3 across 272 classification datasets, combining representation geometry, prediction trajectories, truncation, and structural interventions, while also examining related representation dynamics in four additional TFMs. We uncover a pronounced expansion-compression trajectory, with stronger late dimensional contraction associated with larger increases in class-prototype separation. These findings distinguish predictive accessibility, class stability, and the benefits of continuing computation, supporting an input-dependent assessment of depthwise redundancy in TFMs.

    Agentic AI systems combine model decisions, mutable state, tool calls, and delegation to external agents. We present AgenticRV, a runtime-verification architecture that separates these boundaries from the monitoring formalism. Adapters emit canonical events; each monitor receives its own projection and abstraction; and a decision policy uses normalised verdicts to select a reaction supported by the responsible adapter. We formalise when observations suffice, monitor replacement preserves decisions, and blocking prevents unsafe effects. We also distinguish rejected attempts from completed effects, avoiding the assumption that a blocked request must leave every monitor in a permanent violation state. The Python implementation supports LangGraph, MCP, and A2A. A controlled LangGraph experiment combines an external Reelay temporal monitor with a programmatic report monitor; ablations show why both are needed for the selected requirements.     ENGLISH

    Distilling capable language-model agents into smaller models requires aligning the student's behavior with the teacher's. This raises a fundamental question: at which states and at what granularity should this alignment be performed? Offline imitation provides dense but token-specific supervision and can suffer from state-distribution mismatch. Token-level on-policy distillation (OPD) addresses this mismatch but typically requires teacher token probabilities and compatible tokenization. We argue that semantic actions provide a natural unit of supervision for agent distillation. We introduce ActionOPD, an action-level on-policy distillation method motivated by maximizing expected teacher-action likelihood at student-encountered states. At each such state, ActionOPD samples actions from both the student and a black-box teacher, rewarding student actions according to their semantic agreement with the sampled teacher actions. Through policy optimization, ActionOPD aligns the student's action-level behavior with the teacher's decisions without requiring reproduction of teacher-written reasoning or access to teacher token probabilities. Training Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with two teachers on diverse, curated tool-use tasks yields average gains of 3.3-6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks. ActionOPD scales favorably with student size and teacher capability, without requiring the teacher and student to share a model family or tokenizer. On $\tau^2$-bench, ActionOPD achieves competitive performance against offline distillation and token-level OPD. We further explore Self-ActionOPD with a same-model teacher and privileged context. These results establish ActionOPD as a promising approach to agent distillation.

    Frontier web agents using closed models have high inference and computational costs. Smaller open models can be an alternative, but to be performant, they require training supervision from a human or teacher model. Token-level teacher distillation is not an option for closed teachers as it needs access to the model's logits. The standard approach is to imitate teacher demonstrations offline, but it trains the student on states it has never visited, and in a style it does not write in. We introduce WebKD, where the teacher is the editor of the student's failures. Given a failed episode, the teacher finds the first point of mistake, and rewrites the student's reasoning traces, harness states, and actions from that point onward. The editing reveals that the teacher's corrections can be more surprising to the student than the student's own text. WebKD instead aims to edit minimally. In the data space, the teacher writes each correction in the student's style. In the objective space, the reasoning is weighted by its contribution to the action. A role-asymmetric KL anchor allows the corrected action to move freely while keeping the reasoning near the student's prior. On the TimeWarp benchmark, WebKD students gain about 5.5-10.7 pp over behavior cloning, outcome-reward RL, and teacher editing baselines. The performance transfers to unseen versions and to the live web in the OnlineMind2Web benchmark. WebKD opens a new way of distilling black-box models to improve the capabilities of open-weight web agents.

Reliable retrieval is challenging because evidence spans interleaved threads, channels, and time, with meaning and authority conditioned on the speaker. Neither RAG's independent chunk retrieval nor memory systems' summary-based consolidation can reliably recover such distributed evidence. EGCForest organizes an immutable message log into three complementary forests: a Channel forest for temporal workflows, an Actor forest for speaker-conditioned context, and an Artifact forest for deliverable lifecycles. Cross-view connections are enabled by a Placement Map and sparse structural bridges. Built on this memory backbone, EGCForest retrieves and assembles evidence by jointly leveraging message-level relevance, hierarchical context from forest summaries, and cross-view links, recovering distributed evidence.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    We propose DeltaStreamer, a novel agentic framework for streaming video understanding inspired by how humans observe, remember, and investigate. Streaming video understanding requires a system to retain evidence before knowing which details future queries will need. Existing approaches often obscure event transitions and omit relevant details when compressing video history, and cannot recover missing visual evidence. DeltaStreamer addresses these limitations by combining change-aware memory with query-driven planning and targeted evidence gathering with replay. Before a query arrives, it continuously observes the stream and explicitly records visual changes in structured memory, preserving how events unfold rather than only what is present. When a query arrives, a query-driven planner identifies the required evidence and guides memory retrieval and targeted replay. By revisiting historical frames, the agent can recover visual details omitted during observation and ground its answer in evidence beyond the retained descriptions. This connects continuous observation with active investigation tailored to each question.     Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Majority Voting (MV) is a simple and widely used strategy which improves the reasoning accuracy of Large Language Models (LLMs) by allocating additional inference-time computation. Specifically, in MV multiple Chain-of-Thoughts (CoTs) are independently sampled and the most frequent final answer is selected. In this work, we propose Length-Conditioned Majority Voting (LCMV), a Test-Time Training approach which improves MV leveraging an empirical observation that has recently been established in several studies: longer CoTs tend to be associated with a lower probability of correctness. We formulate this inductive bias as a length-conditioned prior probability, which is modeled by a simple logistic function. Moreover, we adapt this prior at test time using only unlabeled testing data and without fine-tuning the LLM. Finally, the adapted prior is used to weight the vote of each sampled answer. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and reasoning benchmarks show that LCMV consistently improves over both standard MV and existing length-based and confidence-based aggregation strategies, while retaining the simplicity and model-agnostic nature of MV. Our code is available at: https://github.com/aimagelab/LCMV.

    多数投票（MV）是一种简单且广泛使用的策略，它通过分配额外的推理时计算来提高大型语言模型（LLM）的推理准确率。具体而言，MV 会独立采样多个思维链（CoT），并选择出现频率最高的最终答案。在这项工作中，我们提出长度条件多数投票（LCMV），这是一种测试时训练方法，它利用近期多项研究确立的一项经验观察来改进 MV：较长的 CoT 往往对应较低的正确概率。我们将这一归纳偏置表述为长度条件先验概率，并用一个简单的逻辑函数对其建模。此外，我们仅使用无标签测试数据在测试时调整该先验，无需对 LLM 进行微调。最后，使用调整后的先验为每个采样答案的投票赋权。在多个 LLM 和推理基准上的大量实验表明，LCMV 持续优于标准 MV，以及现有基于长度和基于置信度的聚合策略，同时保留了 MV 的简洁性和模型无关特性。代码地址：https://github.com/aimagelab/LCMV。

    Miko{\l}aj Pi\'orczy\'nski, Wojciech Masarczyk, Damian S\'ojka, Sebastian Cygert, Bart{\l}omiej Twardowski

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper analyzes why representation-based test-time adaptation fails, linking MLLM corruption robustness to the geometry of visual-token shifts and bounding single-site, sample-blind corrections. This is transferable representation-geometry insight; adaptation and multimodal-model context alone do not establish contributions to composition, reasoning, or systems.

    本文分析基于表征的测试时适应为何会失败，将 MLLM 对损坏的鲁棒性与视觉词元偏移的几何结构联系起来，并界定单点、不依赖样本的校正所能达到的上限。这提供了可迁移的表征几何见解；仅凭适应方法和多模态模型背景，并不能证明其对组合性、推理或系统领域有所贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Vision-language models suffer significant accuracy drops under common corruptions. While test-time adaptation (TTA) successfully mitigates these shifts in CLIP-like contrastive models, its application to generative multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains underexplored and uniquely challenging due to their sequential token generation. In this work, we demonstrate that representation-based TTA fails to recover performance in MLLMs. Our experiments reveal that even when violating standard TTA assumptions by leveraging target data offline, sample-blind feature alignment recovers only marginal accuracy. We attribute this failure to the nature of corruption shifts: unlike CLIP-like architectures, which benefit from a shared domain-shift direction within a single pooled classification embedding, MLLM visual token sequence shifts are nearly orthogonal and span the full embedding space.These findings bound what any sample-blind, position-shared correction at a single encoder site can achieve, establishing that representation-space interventions alone might be insufficient to ensure corruption robustness in MLLMs.

    中文

    视觉语言模型在常见损坏下会出现显著的准确率下降。测试时适应（TTA）已成功缓解 CLIP 类对比模型中的此类偏移，但由于生成式多模态大型语言模型（MLLM）需要按顺序生成词元，将 TTA 应用于这类模型仍缺乏充分研究，并面临独特挑战。在这项工作中，我们证明基于表征的 TTA 无法恢复 MLLM 的性能。实验表明，即使通过离线利用目标数据而违背标准 TTA 假设，不依赖样本的特征对齐所恢复的准确率也仅有小幅提升。我们将这一失败归因于损坏偏移的性质：与能从单个池化分类嵌入中的共享域偏移方向受益的 CLIP 类架构不同，MLLM 视觉词元序列的偏移几乎彼此正交，并且覆盖整个嵌入空间。这些发现界定了在单个编码器位置进行的任何不依赖样本、跨位置共享的校正所能达到的上限，并表明仅靠表征空间干预可能不足以确保 MLLM 对损坏具有鲁棒性。

    Universal Sample-Based Embeddings of Higher-Order Objects

    高阶对象的通用基于样本的嵌入

    Radovan Halu\v{s}ka, Christopher Solinas, Nathan R. Sturtevant, Martin Schmid, Michael Bowling

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper proposes sample-based fixed-size embeddings that generalize across families of higher-order objects, with evidence across distributions, functions, and graphs. This substantially advances reusable representations and transfer to unseen objects, but does not study internal model mechanisms; downstream problem-solving is demonstrated rather than being the central contribution.

    本文提出基于样本的固定大小嵌入，能够在分布、函数和图等对象族之间泛化，并提供了相应证据。这显著推进了可复用表征及其向未见对象的迁移，但没有研究模型内部机制；下游问题求解是展示用途，而非核心贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Neural networks operate naturally on finite-dimensional vectors, yet many problems require reasoning about higher-order objects such as distributions, functions, and graphs. Such objects capture relationships within a ground set and rarely admit an explicit compact representation. Moreover, we typically want a compact representation not of a single higher-order object but of an entire family of such objects, including members unseen during training. While a few approaches exist for particular object types, none is designed to work across object types. We propose a unified framework that represents any higher-order object as a fixed-size embedding vector learned over a family of such objects. An encoder maps an object, seen only through a finite set of samples, to an embedding, and a domain-specific decoder supplies the training signal by modeling the object conditioned on that embedding. Since the encoder works only from samples, one architecture serves different object types. Because the decoder is a model already suited to single instances of the object type, the framework inherits that model's native operations and inductive biases. We instantiate the framework on distributions, functions, and graphs. In each case we show that a single trained model represents an entire family and generalizes to members unseen during training. Furthermore, we demonstrate the downstream utility of these embeddings: interpolating distributions in embedding space, solving differential equations in embedding space, and predicting unseen edges from a graph's embedding.

    中文

    神经网络天然适用于有限维向量，但许多问题需要对分布、函数和图等高阶对象进行推理。这类对象刻画了一个底集中的关系，而且很少能用显式的紧凑表示来表示。此外，我们通常希望紧凑表示的不是单个高阶对象，而是这类对象的整个族，包括训练期间未见过的成员。尽管针对特定对象类型已有少数方法，但没有一种方法旨在跨对象类型通用。我们提出一个统一框架，将任意高阶对象表示为在一族此类对象上学习得到的固定大小嵌入向量。编码器仅通过有限样本观察对象，并将其映射为嵌入；特定领域的解码器则通过对给定嵌入条件下的对象建模来提供训练信号。由于编码器仅依赖样本工作，因此同一种架构可服务于不同对象类型。由于解码器本身就是适用于该对象类型单个实例的模型，该框架继承了该模型原有的操作方式和归纳偏置。我们将该框架应用于分布、函数和图。在每种情况下，我们都表明，单个训练好的模型能够表示一个完整的对象族，并泛化到训练期间未见过的成员。此外，我们还展示了这些嵌入的下游用途：在嵌入空间中插值分布、求解微分方程，以及根据图的嵌入预测未见过的边。

    Yanyi Su, Yu Zeng, Hongshuai Wang, Chenyan Wang, Zhifeng Gao, Xiaohui Yang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper introduces a controlled diagnostic showing that chemical predictions can shift with source-entity identity, exposing limits in claims of transferable structure-property reasoning. It substantially advances reasoning evaluation, with a partial connection to compositional generalization through structural edits; the application context alone gives no substantive connection to interpretability or systems.

    本文提出一项受控诊断，表明化学预测可能随源实体身份而变化，从而揭示了关于可迁移结构—性质推理能力的主张所存在的局限。它显著推进了推理能力评估，并通过结构编辑与组合泛化有一定联系；仅凭应用背景，并不能证明其与可解释性或系统领域有实质联系。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    LLMs have achieved strong performance on chemical prediction benchmarks. However, existing evaluation methods typically provide target entity identity information directly, making it difficult to determine whether model predictions arise from transferable structure-property reasoning capabilities or rely on target-related contextual information or memory retrieval. We propose the Identity-Blinded Reasoning Diagnostic framework to evaluate chemical prediction models when target entity identity information is hidden. In this framework, the target is no longer directly defined by its entity identity, but instead by a known source entity and an explicit structural edit operation. This setting preserves the information required to determine the target while reducing the opportunity for models to access target identity cues. We evaluate this framework across six tasks spanning odor prediction, molecular property prediction, retrosynthesis, and reaction yield prediction. The results show that models generally achieve better prediction performance when source and target entity properties are consistent. Providing explicit source entity labels further strengthens this dependence. Moreover, while keeping the target entity, structural change, and ground-truth label unchanged, replacing only the source entity label causes some model predictions to systematically shift toward the substituted source labels. These results indicate that high benchmark accuracy in chemical prediction tasks does not necessarily imply that LLMs possess reliable structure-property reasoning capabilities. Our diagnostic framework provides a controlled evaluation approach for testing whether models can genuinely update predictions according to entity changes. The framework can be extended to other AI for Science tasks, particularly those where targets can be defined through transformations of known entities.

    中文

    LLM 在化学预测基准上取得了出色表现。然而，现有评估方法通常直接提供目标实体的身份信息，因此很难判断模型预测究竟源于可迁移的结构—性质推理能力，还是依赖与目标相关的上下文信息或记忆检索。我们提出身份盲化推理诊断框架，用于在隐藏目标实体身份信息时评估化学预测模型。在该框架中，目标不再由其实体身份直接定义，而是通过已知的源实体和明确的结构编辑操作来定义。这样的设置保留了确定目标所需的信息，同时减少模型获取目标身份线索的机会。我们在六项任务上评估该框架，涵盖气味预测、分子性质预测、逆合成和反应产率预测。结果表明，当源实体和目标实体的性质一致时，模型通常能取得更好的预测表现。提供明确的源实体标签会进一步加剧这种依赖。此外，在保持目标实体、结构变化和真实标签不变的情况下，仅替换源实体标签，就会导致一些模型的预测系统性地转向被替换后的源标签。这些结果表明，化学预测任务上的高基准准确率并不一定意味着 LLM 具备可靠的结构—性质推理能力。我们的诊断框架提供了一种受控评估方法，用于测试模型能否根据实体变化真正更新预测。该框架可扩展到其他 AI for Science 任务，尤其适用于能够通过对已知实体进行变换来定义目标的任务。

    Tao Yu, Zhongtian Luo, Yuchen Long, Yiheng Lu, Yuxuan Zhou, Yanpei Gong, Siyi Cao, Yuqing Wu, Haopeng Jin, Zhenghao Zhang, Yujia Yang, Jingmin Zhu, Yunyun Hou, Xinming Wang, Hongzhu Yi, Jiachen Liu, Sirui Wang, Nan Duan, Yan Huang, Liang Wang, Tianjin Huang, Yanyan Zou

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper benchmarks how ordinary noise during agent skill learning affects later task performance and introduces diagnostics for skill updates, making agent learning and reusable skill systems its main contribution. Reusable skills connect partially to composition, but the abstract does not study compositional generalization or reasoning mechanisms; performance diagnostics alone provide only an incidental interpretability connection.

    本文基准测试普通噪声在智能体技能学习期间如何影响后续任务表现，并提出技能更新诊断方法，因此智能体学习和可复用技能系统是其主要贡献。可复用技能与组合性有一定联系，但摘要没有研究组合泛化或推理机制；性能诊断与可解释性的联系也只是附带的。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language model agents increasingly improve by distilling experience into reusable skills, but errors in that experience can persist in learned rules and affect later tasks. Existing evaluations largely examine clean learning or perturbations encountered after skills are frozen, leaving robustness during self-evolution insufficiently understood. We introduce RSE-Bench, to our knowledge the first benchmark for evaluating skill self-evolution under ordinary, non-adversarial noise. It spans four domains and six benchmarks, with controlled perturbations to instructions, environmental evidence, execution records, and outcome--record pairings that preserve the underlying tasks and native scoring rules. The protocol separates noise during learning from input-side noise at evaluation, testing frozen skill stores on held-out tasks. We also introduce \textsc{RSEClaw}, a method-agnostic framework supporting consistent noise injection and process diagnostics of actual exposure and skill updates. Across three methods and two backbones, noisy learning retains only $25.5\%$--$42.1\%$ of the aggregate gain achieved by clean self-evolution, depending on the noise type. Perturbations confined to execution records and outcome--record pairings cause average losses comparable to input-side noise, despite leaving the original executions and evaluations intact. Diagnostics further identify differences in candidate skill text that coexist with small changes in mean held-out performance.

    中文

    大型语言模型智能体越来越多地通过将经验提炼为可复用技能来提升能力，但这些经验中的错误可能会保留在学得的规则中，并影响后续任务。现有评估大多考察干净学习，或技能冻结后遇到的扰动，因此对自我演化过程中的鲁棒性仍缺乏充分理解。我们提出 RSE-Bench，据我们所知，这是首个用于评估普通非对抗性噪声下技能自我演化的基准。它涵盖四个领域和六个基准，在不改变底层任务和原生评分规则的前提下，对指令、环境证据、执行记录以及结果与记录的配对施加受控扰动。该协议将学习期间的噪声与评估时输入侧的噪声区分开来，并在留出任务上测试冻结的技能库。我们还提出 \textsc{RSEClaw}，这是一个与方法无关的框架，支持一致的噪声注入，并对实际暴露情况和技能更新进行过程诊断。在三种方法和两种骨干模型上，带噪学习仅保留干净自我演化所取得总体增益的$25.5\%$——$42.1\%$，具体比例取决于噪声类型。仅作用于执行记录以及结果与记录配对的扰动，也会造成与输入侧噪声相当的平均损失，尽管原始执行和评估都保持不变。诊断还发现，候选技能文本存在差异，而留出集平均性能的变化却很小。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Molecular design is often formulated as an optimization problem over existing molecular spaces. However, molecular optimization and the discovery of structurally distinct replacement molecules represent two fundamentally different search problems. LLM-based molecular design agents typically perform the former, conducting local refinement within the neighborhood of existing structures to improve target properties through structural modifications. In contrast, the latter requires exploration of a broader chemical space to discover molecules with entirely different scaffolds while preserving the functional characteristics of reference molecules. We propose MolHop, an agentic framework for cross-scaffold molecular discovery that enables models to navigate and edit within a pre-organized chemical space. MolHop organizes approximately 1.6 million molecular scaffolds from commercial molecules into a coarse-to-fine hierarchical action space. The agent selects new exploration regions through scaffold navigation actions and adjusts candidate properties through molecular editing. The framework maintains historical trajectory memory to support long-horizon search processes. On drug molecule and commercial compound tasks, connecting Grok-4.6 and DeepSeek-Flash-V4.1 to the MolHop framework substantially improves their cross-scaffold joint success rates. We develop MolHop-9B through agentic reinforcement learning, and MolHop-9B outperforms generative baselines including GPT-5.6-sol, Claude-5-Opus, and Gemini-3.1-Pro, while generating candidate molecules with larger scaffold differences from the reference molecules. These results demonstrate that effective molecular discovery beyond the traditional optimization paradigm requires structured chemical and action spaces, enabling agents to explore new structural regions rather than merely refine existing molecules.

    The paper trains a reinforcement-learning controller to choose which video frames enter a tracker’s memory, improving benchmark performance across model generations. This is a substantial memory-control contribution to model systems; tracking performance alone offers only an incidental connection to reasoning and none to interpretability or compositional generalization.

    本文训练了一个强化学习控制器，以选择哪些视频帧进入跟踪器的记忆，从而提升跨模型代际的基准表现。这是对模型系统中记忆控制的一项重要贡献；仅凭跟踪性能，与推理的联系只是附带的，与可解释性或组合泛化则没有联系。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) is a foundation model for image and video segmentation that sets the state of the art in visual object tracking. Its tracker, inherited from SAM 2, stores information from past frames in a memory bank, managed by a simple First-In-First-Out rule, allowing temporal consistency in complex videos. Several recent methods improve SAM 2 with hand-crafted memory update rules, each targeting a specific failure mode, such as distractors, occlusions, or object motion. However, their gains transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone. We instead present a more general, data-driven approach that frames memory control as a sequential decision-making task. SAM3RL is an extension of the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller, trained by reinforcement learning, that decides which frames enter the memory bank in order to maximize tracking performance. SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without any runtime overhead. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL, which outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks, showing the generality of our method across model generations.

    Amartya Banerjee, Xingyu Xu, Caroline Moosm\"uller, Harlin Lee

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper introduces finite-horizon energy learning for graph generation, including an unbiased acceptance-gradient estimator and improved terminal-sample quality at fixed budgets. This is a substantial algorithmic contribution to generative computation, but the abstract does not address interpretability, compositional generalization, or reasoning.

    本文提出用于图生成的有限时域能量学习，其中包括一个无偏的接受梯度估计器，并在固定预算下改善终端样本质量。这是对生成计算的一项重要算法贡献，但摘要没有涉及可解释性、组合泛化或推理。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Energy-based models can represent distributions over discrete structures such as molecular graphs, but an energy that is accurate at equilibrium need not yield accurate samples when the sampler stops after a fixed number of steps. We introduce finite-horizon energy learning, which adapts the acceptance energy of a Metropolis--Hastings sampler to the distribution it returns after a prescribed number of steps, with initialization, proposals, and annealing schedule held fixed. For graph generation, a frozen pretrained model supplies initialization and proposals, and a learned energy governs acceptance. A training-only discriminator scores completed samples, and coupled continuations of the accepted and rejected branches of a proposal give an acceptance-gradient estimator that is unbiased for a fixed discriminator under stated conditions, without equilibrated negative samples or differentiation through discrete states. Generation uses the learned energy in the original single-trajectory sampler, without discriminator evaluations or reranking. On twelve pairwise binary targets with exactly evaluated terminal laws, learned energies have lower median terminal total variation than the equilibrium-correct energy in every tested short-horizon setting, and than its numerically tuned scalar multiple in most settings. On MOSES, a learned two-coefficient combination of pretrained Graph Energy Matching (GEM) potentials lowers FCD by 3.7--10.5\% relative to scale-calibrated GEM at matched sampling steps, with validity gains at the shortest budget and a sub-point validity trade-off at higher budgets.

    Agent skills adapt frozen models through editable external instructions. Revising several rules at once makes changes difficult to inspect, while judging each local edit only by its immediate score can discard useful intermediate states. We introduce AtomSearch, which keeps revision actions local while using subsequent skill states to guide search. Contrastive atomic editing links each primitive rule edit to failed and successful executions, a behavioral hypothesis, and an intended scope. Skill-State Tree Search (STS) evaluates short edit compositions and selectively retains them as executable states that can be revisited and extended. Outcome memory supplies later proposals with observed repair and regression statistics. We evaluate AtomSearch across four tasks and five target models. With deepseek-v4-flash, it exceeds SkillOpt on three of four tasks, including a 9.68-percentage-point gain on LiveMathematicianBench, and SkillOpt's final skills contain 2.3-19.7 times as many characters. In 67% of completed searches, the best validation state passes through an ancestor that was not highest-scoring at its depth. These results show how local rule edits can support the exploration of useful revision paths and yield compact skills, with additional offline evaluations used to explore alternative states.

    ENGLISH

    World models aim to learn compact representations of an environment from observations, enabling agents to predict future states and plan their behaviour. However, most existing approaches learn black-box representations, with limited ability to incorporate prior knowledge about the world. We introduce Concept-Grounded World Models (CGWMs), a neurosymbolic world model design that instead learns interpretable concept representations. We learn these concepts from observations using explicit and complete knowledge, expressed in temporal logic, that specifies the valid world states and the temporal relations governing their dynamics. Furthermore, we directly use this knowledge by formulating planning as differentiable reasoning, optimising the agent's actions by gradient ascent to satisfy a goal. We experimentally compare CGWM with a purely neural baseline and a neurosymbolic baseline on two game environments. We find that CGWMs ground concepts much more accurately, even over long horizons, resulting in significantly more robust planning both in and out of distribution.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Federated fine-tuning enables large language models (LLMs) to learn collaboratively from distributed client data, but malicious client updates can compromise global model safety. As federated tasks evolve, changing malicious update patterns challenge the ability of existing defenses to maintain reliable risk detection over time. To address this challenge, we propose Safe-FCL, a framework integrating continual risk awareness with fine-grained safety aggregation for federated continual learning of LLMs. Specifically, the Continual Risk Awareness (CRA) mechanism learns emerging risk patterns across sequential tasks and constrains detector updates using a protective subspace derived from historical features, mitigating forgetting of previously learned malicious patterns while adapting to new risks. To translate risk awareness into aggregation-level safety control, the Fine-Grained Safety Aggregation (FGSA) mechanism combines client-level risk assessments from CRA with module-level deviations from historical update behavior to adaptively regulate aggregation contributions, suppressing potentially malicious updates while minimizing unnecessary restrictions on benign updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Safe-FCL outperforms current SOTA methods, improving global-model Rule and MD-Judge scores in federated continual learning by 0.41% and 0.64%, respectively, while increasing average risk recognition accuracy by 2.01%.

    Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under matched budgets. Prior work demonstrates that different loop visits can play different roles even when they share parameters. To probe the contributions of different loop visits, we learn separate residual coefficients in a model that applies a shared block twice, observing a smaller scale in the first visit. Fixed coefficient experiments show that reducing the first visit's scale preserves or improves performance, whereas the same reductions to the second hurt it. This asymmetry motivates us to explore asymmetric compute allocation. We propose \textbf{LatentLoop}, which compresses the first visit's sequence, retains full resolution in the second, and reallocates saved computation to increase the hidden size. We further learn how strongly the first visit updates the full sequence, and share MoE weights across visits while using separate attention parameters to accommodate their different sequence resolutions. Across 15 configurations spanning 1.3B--7B parameters, with the largest budget exceeding $10^{21}$ FLOPs, LatentLoop consistently lowers validation NLL. At a fitted NLL of 1.988, predicted compute savings are 19.0\% and 7.9\% relative to vanilla MoE and the looped baseline. It also improves average scores on nine benchmarks at all sizes in 0-shot and 5-shot settings. These results suggest asymmetric compute allocation is a promising direction for looped MoE models.

    Mario Mallea, Angela Nebot, Franscisco Mugica

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper empirically maps ESN performance on synthetic sequence tasks and contributes input modulation and shared readout mechanisms that improve structural pattern tasks, giving transferable insight into composition and generalization. Its analysis of memory and reservoir dynamics is relevant to model mechanisms, but does not directly investigate internal representations; sequence problem solving and recurrent architecture are secondary connections.

    本文实证刻画 ESN 在合成序列任务上的性能，并提出输入调制和共享读出机制，以改进结构性模式任务，从而为组合与泛化提供可迁移的见解。对记忆和储备池动态的分析与模型机制相关，但并未直接研究内部表征；序列问题求解和循环架构只是次要关联。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Efficient sequence modeling remains a fundamental challenge in machine learning. Despite the success of Transformers, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have recently re-emerged as efficient alternatives. Particularly, Echo State Networks (ESNs) offer a compelling framework of randomized RNNs that have been extensively studied for time-series forecasting and dynamical systems. This paper presents an empirical analysis of distributional, architectural, and optimization variants of ESNs evaluated on few-shot sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) pattern tasks. These synthetic tasks utilize discrete symbol sequences, characterized by delays, inactive phases, and triggered markers to isolate and evaluate memory and pattern recognition capabilities. The minimality of these tasks is crucial to understand the strengths and limitations of machine learning models. Furthermore, when the input signal utilizes a one-hot encoding, ESN dynamics are governed strictly by their weight distributions, offering an ideal lens through which to study reservoir computing. Our findings map the performance boundaries of ESNs relative to state-of-the-art (SOTA) models. We show that preserving a linear state regime is vital for memory tasks, such as pattern completion or simple copy. We propose a data-dependent modulation mechanism for nonlinear input injection into the reservoir (G-ESN). G-ESN functions as a statistical filter capable of solving tasks that conventional ESNs cannot (the adding problem and bracket matching). Finally, for Deep ESNs, we evaluate a shared readout mechanism across layers that outperforms conventional concatenated readouts on structural tasks, including selective copy, sorting problem, and bracket matching.

    Progress toward general intelligence in the physical world requires scaling robot learning across diverse environments and interactions. However, existing robot policies use shared parameters that remain fixed across interaction contexts. When different operations favor competing parameter adjustments, fitting their mixture can leave individual operations insufficiently adapted. Our atomic-task diagnostics reveal competing update directions in both vision-language and action parameters, with source-improving updates increasing loss on other tasks. This motivates MorphAct, a contextual parameterization framework that dynamically adjusts robot policy parameters as interaction contexts change. Two coupled generators produce context-dependent low-rank updates for the vision-language and action modules. Their coupling follows the policy's computational dependency: vision-language updates shape the representations that condition action-side parameter generation. Both generators are trained jointly through the native action objective, without operation labels or expert-adapter targets.     Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    Using known simulator ground truth, the study shows that next-token pretraining learns amortized Bayesian inference over market regimes, including filtering drifting latent states, and that training-regime diversity supports transfer. Decoding the regime from frozen activations provides substantial evidence about learned representations, though the paper does not directly investigate circuits or feature organization; generalization and inference are present but secondary to its focus on what the model learns.

    利用已知的模拟器真实情况，本文表明下一个 token 预训练能够学会针对市场状态的摊销贝叶斯推断，包括对漂移潜在状态进行滤波；训练状态的多样性则有助于迁移。从冻结激活中解码状态为学得的表征提供了有力证据，但本文并未直接研究回路或特征组织；泛化和推断虽有涉及，却是次于“模型学到了什么”这一关注点的内容。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Autoregressive transformers trained on limit order book (LOB) message streams are increasingly proposed as foundation models for market microstructure. Because the generative process of real markets is unknown, these models can be judged only by the realism of their output, leaving open what they actually learn. We make the question answerable by inverting the setup: we train GPT-style models on order flow from simulators whose latent parameters are known, so that the Bayes-optimal predictor, the generating state, and the exact data entropy serve as references. Measured against them, next-token pretraining on order flow implements amortized Bayesian inference over market regimes. The learned predictive matches the exact Bayes optimum to within a millinat per token and approaches the oracle floor even on a nonstationary family whose latent state drifts within an episode, a regime that requires filtering. The latent regime is linearly decodable from frozen activations, well above baselines, so a frozen-model read-out calibrates simulator parameters more accurately than windowed maximum likelihood at a fraction of the cost. In our experiments these capabilities are not produced by scale: capacity and token volume saturate early, and it is the diversity of training regimes, not the token count, that determines generalization to unseen markets. On real NASDAQ data, zero-shot transfer is set by how well the simulator prior covers real flow: an enriched mixture nearly closes the gap to an in-domain baseline, and pretraining beats from-scratch training at every budget across held-out tickers. Known ground truth turns average next-token loss, which is uninformative near the entropy floor, into an exact comparison against the Bayes-optimal and oracle predictors.

    中文

    在限价订单簿（LOB）消息流上训练的自回归 Transformer，日益被用于构建市场微观结构基础模型。由于真实市场的生成过程未知，人们只能根据其输出的逼真程度来评判这些模型，因此它们究竟学到了什么仍不得而知。我们通过反转这一设定，使这个问题变得可回答：我们在潜在参数已知的模拟器所生成的订单流上训练 GPT 式模型，并以贝叶斯最优预测器、生成状态和精确数据熵作为参照。与这些参照相比，在订单流上进行的下一个 token 预训练实现了对市场状态的摊销贝叶斯推断。模型学得的预测结果与精确贝叶斯最优预测每个 token 相差不到一个毫纳特；即使在潜在状态会于一个 episode 内漂移、因而需要进行滤波的非平稳族上，预测结果也接近 oracle 下限。潜在状态可从冻结激活中线性解码，表现远优于基线；因此，基于冻结模型的读出可以用极低成本，比窗口化最大似然更准确地校准模拟器参数。在我们的实验中，这些能力并非由规模带来：模型容量和 token 数量很早便趋于饱和，而决定对未见市场泛化能力的是训练状态的多样性，而非 token 数量。在真实 NASDAQ 数据上，零样本迁移效果取决于模拟器先验对真实订单流的覆盖程度：扩充后的混合分布几乎弥合了与域内基线之间的差距，并且在所有预算下，预训练在留出的股票代码上都优于从头训练。已知的真实情况使平均下一个 token 损失能够转化为与贝叶斯最优预测器和 oracle 预测器之间的精确比较；当损失接近熵下限时，单看该指标并无信息。

Plug-in decision heads on a frozen generator predict the action type, pool the visual tokens inside each numbered box to pick the target, and point at a listed text option or at a WRITE slot that leaves the writing of new text to the generator. With Qwen3-VL 4B and 8B generators trained on 213k web steps, a strict threshold keeps the cascade between 0.3 points below and 1.4 points above the generator on seven offline test sets while the heads decide 12 to 64% of the steps. A looser threshold raises step success on unseen Mind2Web websites by 3.1 and 1.8 points, costs up to 2 points on GUIAct and MiniWoB++, and lifts WebArena task success from 12.5 to 13.8% (4B) and from 13.6 to 14.6% (8B) with less than half of the generated tokens.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Long coding agent sessions outgrow the model's context window, so agents compact: older history is replaced by something shorter, usually a model-written summary. A summary selects and rewords, and the agent cannot see what was lost. Existing work has explored a range of compaction techniques, but comparatively little attention has been paid to their effectiveness with lightweight models, including those deployed locally or used for high-volume workloads. Here, we present transparent-compact, a simple deterministic method for the open-source Pi coding agent, designed specifically for use with such models and with the purpose of maximising the transparency of the agent's view of its own compacted context. It guarantees that user and assistant prose in its context is unchanged by a model or algorithm, and explicitly flags where compaction has stripped information. We compare it with Pi's default model-written summary compaction and with pi-vcc, a popular deterministic method with similar methods but without verbatim retention of prose. Our benchmarks run on four models of varying performance levels, with emphasis on Qwen3.8-27B: a lightweight model at the top end of what consumer hardware can serve locally. On sets probing commitments (rules the user set which exist only in the conversation) and recall of facts, transparent-compact matched or outperformed both alternatives. In particular, it showed an advantage in avoiding confident blunders, i.e. assertion of false information as opposed to recognizing that something was not recalled. Even with a frontier model, its advantage was present but smaller. We argue that transparent-compact spares lightweight models from reasoning or searching their way around what compaction lost, and results in improved recall and application of information as a result, without the need for task or context-specific structuring of the session history.

    长时间运行的编码智能体会超出模型的上下文窗口，因此智能体会进行压缩：用更短的内容替换较早的历史记录，通常是由模型撰写的摘要。摘要会筛选并改写内容，而智能体无法看到哪些信息丢失了。现有研究探索了多种压缩技术，但相对较少关注这些技术对轻量级模型的效果，包括本地部署或用于高负载工作场景的模型。在此，我们为开源 Pi 编码智能体提出 transparent-compact，这是一种简单的确定性方法，专为此类模型设计，旨在最大限度提高智能体对自身压缩后上下文的视图透明度。它保证上下文中的用户和助手文本不会被模型或算法改动，并明确标出压缩剔除了信息的位置。我们将其与 Pi 默认的模型撰写摘要压缩方法，以及一种流行的确定性方法 pi-vcc 进行比较；后者采用了类似方法，但不会逐字保留文本。我们的基准测试涵盖性能水平各异的四种模型，重点考察 Qwen3.8-27B：这是一种轻量级模型，处于消费级硬件可本地运行的模型上限。在考察承诺（用户设定、仅存在于对话中的规则）和事实回忆的测试集上，transparent-compact 的表现持平或优于另外两种方法。具体而言，它在避免自信地犯错方面表现更好，也就是避免断言错误信息，而非承认自己没有回忆起来。即使使用前沿模型，它仍有优势，但幅度较小。我们认为，transparent-compact 使轻量级模型不必再通过推理或搜索来弥补压缩造成的信息损失，从而改善信息回忆与应用；同时，无需针对任务或上下文对会话历史进行特定结构化处理。

    Parallel drafters such as DFlash and DSpark reduce proposal latency, but early mismatches limit how much of each block can be accepted. Retaining alternatives introduces parent states and candidate choices that reference-conditioned training does not directly supervise. We introduce TreeSpark, a unified training and inference framework extending the semi-autoregressive DSpark architecture. It constructs parent-conditioned candidate trees from one backbone pass and replays their expansion, pruning, and budgeted packing during training. Survival negative log-likelihood weights retained edges by reference-derived path mass, while a capped coverage hinge promotes target-important alternatives near local selection boundaries. Both objectives reuse reference-chain target distributions without additional target forward passes. We evaluate greedy decoding with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B on nine general benchmarks and six writing domains. Across targets and suites, TreeSpark improves mean acceptance length over DSpark by 23.4% to 31.6% and mean single-request throughput by 15.1% to 25.0%. Batched Qwen3-4B throughput improves by 12.6% to 17.2%. At fixed attention capacity and inference policy, the proposed supervision further improves mean acceptance length by approximately 6.4% and mean system throughput by 4.2% to 5.0% on Qwen3-4B.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Probes on activation vectors are widely used to detect misbehavior in language models, but their success relies on the assumption that models cannot control what their activations encode. Humans can learn, through neurofeedback, to control the firing of even single neurons, and recent studies investigated whether this ability extends to language models, reaching conflicting conclusions. No experimental design so far disentangles competence at the task from genuine access to one's own activations. We fill this gap with in-context neurofeedback sessions, in which a "subject" model is asked to maximize (or minimize) a score derived from its activations, shown back to it at every turn. In our first experiment, the sentences are generated either by the subject or by a second "writer" model, while the score always derives from the activations of the subject. We test ten open-weight models from five families, with sizes from 9B to 32B. Some models move their own scores considerably, but no more than a writer of comparable competence moves them. Is this because the task requires no privileged access, or because the subject controls its activations while processing the sentences, whoever wrote them? To answer this, we prefill a fixed sentence as the subject's reply at every turn and ask it to increase or decrease the score. Three out of ten models show small but consistent control effects. We further ask whether models can control their activations to the point of fooling an activation monitor. We make models repeat sentences a monitor would flag, such as a deceptive answer for a deception monitor, and ask them to raise or lower the monitor's score. No model learns to lower it, but one model can raise it. In-context control of a model's own activations might not yet be a threat to activation monitors, but it exists in a few models and needs to be tracked as models evolve.

    中文

    基于激活向量的探针被广泛用于检测语言模型的不当行为，但其有效性依赖于一个假设：模型无法控制其激活所编码的内容。人类可以通过神经反馈学会控制神经元的放电，甚至能够控制单个神经元；近期研究探讨了这种能力是否也适用于语言模型，但得出了相互矛盾的结论。迄今为止，还没有实验设计能够将任务能力与真正访问自身激活的能力区分开来。我们通过上下文内神经反馈环节填补这一空白：在每一轮中，都会向一个“受试”模型展示一个由其激活计算得出的分数，并要求它最大化（或最小化）该分数。在第一个实验中，句子由受试模型或另一个“写作者”模型生成，而分数始终根据受试模型的激活计算。我们测试了来自五个系列的十种开放权重模型，规模从 9B 到 32B。有些模型能显著改变自身分数，但其改变幅度并不超过能力相当的写作者模型。这究竟是因为任务不需要特殊访问权限，还是因为无论句子由谁撰写，受试模型在处理句子时都能控制自身激活？为回答这个问题，我们在每一轮都将一个固定句子预填充为受试模型的回复，并要求它提高或降低分数。十种模型中有三种表现出幅度较小但一致的控制效应。我们进一步考察模型能否控制激活，达到欺骗激活监测器的程度。我们让模型重复监测器会标记的句子，例如欺骗监测器所针对的欺骗性回答，并要求它提高或降低监测器分数。没有模型学会降低分数，但有一种模型能提高分数。上下文内控制模型自身激活的能力或许尚未对激活监测器构成威胁，但这种能力确实存在于少数模型中，并且随着模型发展需要持续跟踪。

    What Makes a Social Agent's Interactions Effective? Learning from Verifiable Outcomes in Paired Worlds

    是什么让社交智能体的互动有效？从成对世界中的可验证结果中学习

    Caixin Kang, Ke Wang, Yuchuan Wu, Xiaoqiang Wang, Ling Li, Bingxue Qiu, Yongbin Li, Yoichi Sato

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    HICO-Bench evaluates whether paired agents reach plans consistent with private conditions, and PaCPO uses cross-scenario tentative plans to assign turn-level credit from end-of-conversation outcomes. This is a substantial contribution to training social reasoning (Reasoning 4) and offers partial evidence about composing plans under changing constraints (CompGen 3) and agent interaction design (Systems 3); it does not study internal representations.

    HICO-Bench 评估成对智能体能否达成符合私有条件的计划，PaCPO 则利用跨场景的暂定计划，根据对话结束时的结果为每一轮分配信用。这对社会推理训练作出了重要贡献（Reasoning 4），也为在约束变化时组合计划（CompGen 3）和智能体交互设计（Systems 3）提供了部分证据；本文未研究内部表征。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Effective social interaction requires more than fluent responses: agents must reach plans that fit the participants' needs and circumstances. Existing evaluations of social agents mainly rely on LLM judges that rate the conversation, without checking the resulting plan. We introduce HICO-Bench, a benchmark of 180 everyday coordination scenarios, such as resource allocation, scheduling, and authorization, in which two agents with private information converse and then independently record the plan they agreed on. A program checks Feasibility (the two records match and satisfy both participants' private conditions), and an LLM judge checks Integrity (the conversation supports the recorded plan); passing both is a Verified Success. Each scenario has two versions that share the same public context but differ in one private condition, so the correct plan differs between them. Across thirteen LLMs, 36% of conversations rated highly for goal completion fail Verified Success. To learn from outcomes that arrive only at the end of a conversation, we propose Paired-Credit Policy Optimization (PaCPO). After each turn, PaCPO asks the agent for a tentative plan, checks it in both versions of the scenario, and rewards the turns after which the tentative plans fit their respective versions. PaCPO raises Qwen3-8B's Verified Success from 20.4% to 28.3%.

    中文

    有效的社交互动不仅需要流畅的回应：智能体还必须达成符合参与者需求和实际情况的计划。现有社交智能体评估主要依赖 LLM 评审员给对话打分，却不检查最终计划。我们提出 HICO-Bench，这是一个包含 180 个日常协调场景的基准，例如资源分配、日程安排和授权。在这些场景中，两个拥有私有信息的智能体进行对话，随后分别记录它们达成一致的计划。程序会检查可行性（两份记录是否一致，并满足双方各自的私有条件），LLM 评审员则检查完整性（对话是否支持所记录的计划）；两项均通过即为验证成功。每个场景都有两个版本，它们共享相同的公开背景，但有一项私有条件不同，因此正确计划也不同。在对十三种 LLM 的评估中，目标完成度评分很高的对话有 36% 未能通过验证成功。为从只能在对话结束时获得的结果中学习，我们提出成对信用策略优化（PaCPO）。每一轮之后，PaCPO 都会要求智能体给出一个暂定计划，在场景的两个版本中分别进行检查，并奖励那些使暂定计划符合各自版本条件的轮次。PaCPO 将 Qwen3-8B 的验证成功率从 20.4% 提升至 28.3%。

    Isabel Jones, Matthew Edwards, Janina A. Hoffmann

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The study identifies traits and network conditions that drive consensus in LLM collectives, giving empirical insight into agent behavior and system organization. Its focus on coordination is only incidental to general reasoning or compositional generalization, and it does not analyze internal model representations.

    这项研究找出了影响 LLM 集体达成共识的特质和网络条件，为智能体行为与系统组织提供了实证见解。其对协调的关注与一般推理或组合泛化仅有间接联系，也未分析模型内部表征。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent environments that produce unanimous agreement, both in intended interactions that need coordination and in unintended emergent interactions. Consequently, understanding how LLMs with competing incentives reach consensus is crucial to better interpret and design LLM collectives. We introduce an evaluation, based on the Network Consensus game, to assess the mechanisms driving this process. Here, a network of agents must agree on one of two colours to receive a payoff, but agents are offered different payoffs for the agreed colour. We vary components such as communication access and network structure and assess six open-source models and one closed model (ChatGPT 5.6-sol). We find that open-source LLMs reach consensus less often than humans in comparable experiments and only if messages are communicated across the global network. ChatGPT 5.6-sol, however, is able to reach consensus with communication limited to its neighbours and with no communication ability. This is achieved through lower stubbornness and higher majority-following tendencies, and by providing more information about its neighbours' states in messages. However, situating agents in a highly clustered graph reduces consensus, regardless of these traits, demonstrating that both system design and individual model traits drive collective outcomes.

    中文

    大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被部署在会产生一致同意的多智能体环境中，这既包括需要协调的预期互动，也包括意料之外的涌现互动。因此，了解具有竞争性激励的 LLM 如何达成共识，对于更好地解释和设计 LLM 集体至关重要。我们提出一种基于网络共识博弈的评估方法，用于分析驱动这一过程的机制。在该博弈中，智能体网络必须对两种颜色中的一种达成一致才能获得收益，但对于达成一致的颜色，不同智能体获得的收益各不相同。我们改变通信权限、网络结构等组成因素，并评估六种开源模型和一种闭源模型（ChatGPT 5.6-sol）。我们发现，开源 LLM 达成共识的频率低于可比实验中的人类，而且只有当消息在整个网络中传递时才能达成共识。然而，ChatGPT 5.6-sol 即使只能与邻居通信，甚至完全无法通信，也能够达成共识。这得益于其较低的固执程度、较强的跟随多数倾向，以及在消息中提供更多关于邻居状态的信息。然而，无论具备何种这些特质，将智能体置于高度聚类的图中都会降低共识率，这表明系统设计和单个模型特质都会影响集体结果。

    What and Where in Identifying and Quantifying Conventions in Humans and AI Agents

    识别并量化人类与 AI 智能体中的惯例：惯例是什么，又在哪里发挥作用

    Makoto Fukushima, Tim Puphal

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper measures and causally tests how humans and agents use conventions in Hanabi, finding transferable evidence that meanings reroute across situations and that blocking several situations has a superadditive cost. This strongly informs compositional convention use, with a more limited connection to reasoning and agent behavior; it does not investigate internal model representations.

    本文测量并因果检验人类和智能体如何在 Hanabi 中使用惯例，发现含义会在不同情形间转移，并且阻断多个情形的代价呈超加性。这为组合式惯例使用提供了有力见解，与推理和智能体行为的联系则较有限；本文未研究模型内部表征。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Cooperative success rests in part on implicit communication. Partners converge on conventions: regularities that give an action meaning beyond its direct effect. Yet conventions are usually observed only indirectly: a score drop when partners are swapped shows that a convention existed, but not what it was or where it was used. In the card game Hanabi, the exact probability that a play fails can be computed from the hints received and the cards in view. Players who use conventions succeed more often than this prediction allows; the resulting margin is the convention gap. Off-belief learning provides a hierarchy of agents (levels 1-5) whose first level uses no conventions by construction and whose later levels use progressively more. For humans and these agents on one scale, we ask what the conventions are and where they are used. On what: in two independently collected corpora of human games, humans show a larger gap than every agent level. On the conventions both populations use, however, humans do no better than level 2. The human advantage is concentrated in a situation that no agent level learns to use: hints that point to a card other than the ones they touch. On where: conventions depend on what the player already knows about the card, not on how recently it was hinted, and they are used most in the mid-game; humans use them earlier and later in the game than the agents. In interventions on the agents, blocking a single high-gap situation costs little, because meaning reroutes to other situations, but blocking several together costs far more than the sum of the single costs. Thus, the convention gap turns conventions from an inferred cause of score loss into a measurable, comparable, and causally testable object.

    中文

    合作成功部分取决于隐式交流。参与者会逐渐形成惯例：某些规律使动作具有超出其直接效果的含义。然而，惯例通常只能通过间接方式观察：更换搭档后分数下降，表明惯例确实存在，却无法说明惯例是什么或在哪里发挥作用。在纸牌游戏 Hanabi 中，可以根据收到的提示和可见的牌，精确计算出一次出牌失败的概率。运用惯例的玩家比这一预测所允许的更常获胜；两者之间的差距就是惯例差距。非信念学习提供了一个智能体层级体系（第 1 至第 5 级）：按照构造，第 1 级不使用惯例，之后各级逐步使用更多惯例。我们将人类和这些智能体置于同一尺度上，考察惯例是什么以及在哪里使用。先看惯例是什么：在两个独立收集的人类游戏语料库中，人类表现出的惯例差距都大于所有智能体等级。然而，在双方群体都会使用的惯例上，人类的表现并不优于第 2 级智能体。人类的优势集中于一种没有任何智能体等级学会使用的情形：提示指向的不是被触及的那些牌。再看惯例在哪里发挥作用：惯例取决于玩家已经知道哪些关于牌的信息，而非提示发出距今多久；惯例在游戏中期使用最多。人类在游戏中比智能体更早、更晚地使用惯例。在针对智能体的干预实验中，阻断一种惯例差距较大的情形代价不高，因为含义会转移到其他情形；但同时阻断多种情形的代价远高于各单独代价之和。因此，惯例差距将惯例从一种推断出的失分原因，转化为可测量、可比较且可进行因果检验的对象。

    Robust Counterfactuals for Markov Decision Processes under Statistical and Causal Uncertainties

    统计与因果不确定性下马尔可夫决策过程的稳健反事实推理

    Jessica Lally, Milad Kazemi, Nicola Paoletti

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper develops robust counterfactual inference and minimal-intervention computation for MDPs under statistical and causal uncertainty, supported by analytical bounds and pessimistic value iteration. This substantially advances counterfactual reasoning, while its MDP setting alone does not establish a contribution to AI agent systems or model internals.

    本文针对统计和因果不确定性，开发了用于 MDP 的稳健反事实推断和最小干预计算方法，并以解析界限和悲观价值迭代为支撑。这实质性推进了反事实推理；但仅凭 MDP 这一研究场景，不能说明其对 AI 智能体系统或模型内部机制有所贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Counterfactual reasoning (asking what would have happened, had a decision been different) is a powerful tool for identifying causes of failure and explaining the behaviour of AI systems in sequential decision-making tasks. In Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), two sources of uncertainty complicate counterfactual inference: statistical uncertainty in the MDP transitions when the MDP is estimated from trajectory data, and uncertainty about the unknown causal model, as there are multiple structural causal models (SCMs) compatible with each MDP. Existing work addresses these two challenges in isolation. We address both simultaneously by introducing a framework for partial counterfactual inference in MDPs that is robust to both statistical and causal uncertainty. Our approach provides: 1) closed-form analytical bounds for the counterfactual probabilities that are valid across all SCMs entailed by a given interval MDP (IMDP); 2) a method to compute minimal robust interventions to achieve a desired counterfactual outcome via pessimistic value iteration on the induced counterfactual IMDP. Since the latter is constructed using our analytical bounds, our approach remains efficient and scalable to realistic MDP environments. Experiments across multiple case studies demonstrate our method's robustness and practical utility for identifying minimal sets of actions that, if changed, would have led to improved outcomes.

    中文

    反事实推理（询问如果决策不同，结果会如何）是一种强有力的工具，可用于识别失败原因，并解释 AI 系统在序贯决策任务中的行为。在马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）中，有两个不确定性来源会使反事实推断变得复杂：一是根据轨迹数据估计 MDP 时，MDP 转移中的统计不确定性；二是未知因果模型的不确定性，因为与每个 MDP 相容的结构因果模型（SCM）可能不止一个。现有研究分别处理这两个挑战。我们通过提出一种适用于 MDP 的部分反事实推断框架，同时处理这两类问题，并使其对统计和因果不确定性都具有稳健性。我们的方法提供：（1）反事实概率的闭式解析界限，这些界限对给定区间 MDP（IMDP）所蕴含的所有 SCM 均有效；（2）一种基于诱导反事实 IMDP 上的悲观价值迭代，计算实现预期反事实结果所需最小稳健干预的方法。由于后者利用我们的解析界限构造，因此该方法在现实 MDP 环境中依然高效且可扩展。多个案例研究中的实验展示了该方法的稳健性和实用价值，可用于找出最小行动集合；如果改变这些行动，结果就会更好。

    MAEM: Mitigating Recency Bias via a Replay-Free, Capacity-Controlled Dynamic Mixture of Experts for Class-Incremental Graph Learning

    MAEM：通过无回放、容量受控的动态专家混合缓解类增量图学习中的近因偏差

    Junlin Chen, Wenhao Wang, Junchao Xu, Qingsong Yao, Fei Xue, Li Sun, Xiao Wang, Ruijie Wang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    MAEM contributes a replay-free continual-learning system with capacity-controlled experts and reconstruction-based routing, evaluated on class-incremental graph benchmarks. Its autoencoders are used for routing rather than interpretability, and the abstract does not address compositional generalization or reasoning.

    MAEM 提出一种无回放持续学习系统，采用容量受控的专家和基于重建的路由，并在类增量图基准上进行了评估。其自编码器用于路由而非可解释性，摘要也未涉及组合泛化或推理。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel on graph-structured data but suffer catastrophic forgetting when classes arrive sequentially. In class-incremental graph learning, predictions are often dominated by recently learned classes, causing severe recency bias. Dynamic expansion can isolate knowledge across sessions, but many methods assume task-incremental settings and require task identities at test time to select branches or heads---information unavailable in class-incremental learning. Learnable routers offer an alternative, yet continual fine-tuning the router on new data can bias routing toward recent components. We propose MAEM, a replay-free, capacity-controlled dynamic mixture-of-experts framework for class-incremental graph learning. MAEM builds representations with Simplified Graph Convolution (SGC) and trains a dedicated expert for each new session, then freezes it to protect prior knowledge. For routing without task IDs or a shared trainable router, each expert uses a masked autoencoder (MAE); test nodes are assigned to the expert with the lowest reconstruction error, reducing routing-level recency bias. When the expert pool reaches a fixed capacity, MAEM merges the least-used experts via Git Re-Basin alignment and further distills them into a fused expert using topology-aware pseudo data synthesized from MAE distributions (DeepInversion-style), without storing or revisiting historical graph data. On four class-incremental graph benchmarks, MAEM mitigates recency bias, outperforms strong continual graph learning baselines, and keeps model capacity bounded under strict replay-free learning.

    中文

    图神经网络（GNN）擅长处理图结构数据，但在类别依次到来时会遭遇灾难性遗忘。在类增量图学习中，预测往往受最近学到的类别支配，从而导致严重的近因偏差。动态扩展可以隔离不同会话中的知识，但许多方法假设采用任务增量设置，并要求在测试时提供任务身份来选择分支或输出头；而在类增量学习中，这类信息并不可用。可学习路由器提供了另一种选择，但在新数据上持续微调路由器可能使其倾向于近期组件。我们提出 MAEM，这是一种用于类增量图学习的无回放、容量受控的动态专家混合框架。MAEM 使用简化图卷积（SGC）构建表征，为每个新会话训练一个专用专家，随后将其冻结以保护已有知识。为实现无需任务 ID 或共享可训练路由器的路由，每个专家都使用一个掩码自编码器（MAE）；测试节点被分配给重建误差最低的专家，从而减少路由层面的近因偏差。当专家池达到固定容量时，MAEM 会通过 Git Re-Basin 对齐合并使用最少的专家，并利用从 MAE 分布合成的、具备拓扑感知能力的伪数据（DeepInversion 风格），将它们进一步蒸馏为一个融合专家，整个过程无需存储或重新访问历史图数据。在四个类增量图基准上的实验表明，MAEM 能够缓解近因偏差，优于强有力的持续图学习基线，并在严格的无回放学习条件下保持模型容量有界。

    PAWA contributes a dataset, scalable capture pipeline, and action-conditioned multiplayer world model that predicts shared-world observations using aligned cross-attention. The agent and world-model architecture is a substantial systems contribution, while directional token alignment alone does not establish compositional generalization or interpretability.

    PAWA 提供了一个数据集、可扩展的采集流水线以及动作条件的多人游戏世界模型，该模型通过对齐的交叉注意力来预测共享世界中的观测结果。智能体与世界模型架构是一项重要的系统贡献；但仅凭方向性 token 对齐，尚不能证明模型具备组合泛化能力或可解释性。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    A multiplayer world model must predict how the independent actions of several players change a shared environment, including changes outside a player's current field of view. A point-of-view (POV) video captures such changes only after they enter its field of view, whereas panoramic video records the surroundings in every viewing direction and has served as an intermediate representation of the world state in recent world models. Learning this task therefore requires synchronized POV and panoramic videos of interacting players together with their actions, yet no existing dataset provides this combination in Minecraft, an established testbed in which players act independently in a shared, modifiable 3D world. We present PAWA, a dataset and framework for action-conditioned panoramic multiplayer world modeling. The dataset pairs each player's POV video with world-stabilized panoramic video and aligned actions. Its distributed pipeline decouples CPU gameplay capture from GPU rendering, scales beyond 64 simultaneous players, and re-renders each recorded session under new observation configurations without replaying the gameplay. On this dataset, we develop a dual-tower model that jointly predicts POV and panoramic video and couples the two streams through cross-attention that aligns tokens observing the same direction in a shared world frame. We further introduce a quadratic-phase player encoding that provides many more player codes than existing rotary codes at the same embedding dimension. Experiments show that PAWA outperforms state-of-the-art multiplayer world models in POV prediction quality while also producing high-fidelity panoramic predictions. The dataset and collection pipeline are open source to support further research on multiplayer world models.

    中文

    多人游戏世界模型必须预测多名玩家各自独立的动作如何改变共享环境，包括玩家当前视野之外发生的变化。第一人称视角（POV）视频只有在这些变化进入其视野后才能捕捉到它们，而全景视频会记录各个观看方向上的周围环境，并已在近期的世界模型中用作世界状态的中间表示。因此，学习这项任务需要交互玩家的同步 POV 视频和全景视频及其动作，但在 Minecraft 中尚无现有数据集提供这种组合。Minecraft 是一个成熟的测试平台，玩家可在共享、可修改的 3D 世界中独立行动。我们提出 PAWA，这是一个用于动作条件全景多人游戏世界建模的数据集和框架。该数据集将每位玩家的 POV 视频与稳定于世界坐标系的全景视频及对齐的动作配对。其分布式流水线将 CPU 游戏过程采集与 GPU 渲染解耦，可扩展至 64 名以上同时在线的玩家，并能在不重放游戏过程的情况下，按新的观测配置重新渲染每段录制会话。基于该数据集，我们开发了一种双塔模型，可联合预测 POV 视频和全景视频，并通过交叉注意力耦合两条流，使其对齐于共享世界坐标系中观察同一方向的 token。我们还提出一种二次相位玩家编码，在相同嵌入维度下可提供比现有旋转编码多得多的玩家代码。实验表明，PAWA 在 POV 预测质量上优于最先进的多人游戏世界模型，同时也能生成高保真的全景预测。该数据集和采集流水线以开源形式提供，以支持多人游戏世界模型的后续研究。
